articles.title: Is the stock market open on Thanksgiving and Black Friday?
articles.summary: The New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are closed for these 10 holidays in 2026 and 2027.
articles.body:

The U.S. stock and bond markets will be closed on Thursday, Nov. 26, in observance of Thanksgiving. Trading resumes again on Friday, Nov. 27, or Black Friday, but the markets will close early: The stock market closes at 1 p.m., and the bond market closes around 2 p.m.

The next trading break will come around the Christmas and New Year's holidays.

Cryptocurrency markets are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

In 2026, the stock market will observe 10 holidays, including two early closings. Many stock market holidays are also federal holidays and banking holidays.

The U.S. stock market's regular hours are 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern time, Monday through Friday. The two major U.S. stock exchanges, the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Nasdaq, each observe these trading hours. Both stock exchanges are closed on weekends.

You can still place orders to buy and sell stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) during extended trading hours, but there is added risk. The trading volume is lighter after hours, so prices can be more volatile, and your orders may not execute fully.

If you ever find yourself wondering, "Is the stock market open today?" check out this list of stock market holidays for 2026 and 2027.

The NYSE and Nasdaq will observe the following holidays in 2026:

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 19

Washington's Birthday, aka Presidents' Day: Monday, Feb. 16

Juneteenth National Independence Day: Friday, June 19

Independence Day (observed): Friday, July 3

Both stock exchanges will also close at 1 p.m. Eastern time on these days in 2026:

Friday, Nov. 27 (the day after Thanksgiving, aka Black Friday)

In 2027, the NYSE and Nasdaq will observe these holidays:

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 18

Washington's Birthday, aka Presidents' Day: Monday, Feb. 15

Juneteenth National Independence Day (observed): Friday, June 18

Independence Day (observed): Monday, July 5

Christmas Day (observed): Friday, Dec. 24

In 2027, the NYSE and Nasdaq will close at 1 p.m. Eastern time on this day:

Friday, Nov. 26 (the day after Thanksgiving, aka Black Friday)

In 2028, the NYSE and Nasdaq will observe these holidays:

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 17

Washington's Birthday, aka Presidents' Day: Monday, Feb. 21

Juneteenth National Independence Day: Monday, June 19

*Because New Year's Day falls on a Saturday, Jan. 1, no New's Year's Day holiday is observed.

In 2028, the NYSE and Nasdaq will close at 1 p.m. Eastern time on this day:

Thursday, July 3: (the day before Independence Day)

Friday, Nov. 24: (the day after Thanksgiving, aka Black Friday)

For holidays that fall on the same date each year, like the Fourth of July and Christmas Day, the stock market is closed the Friday before if the holiday falls on a Saturday or the Monday after if it falls on a Sunday.

One exception: If New Year's Day falls on a Saturday, stock exchanges are open for regular hours the Friday before, and the holiday simply isn't observed by Wall Street.

Most American financial markets also close for a National Day of Mourning upon the death of a past or sitting president. Typically, this day is observed on the day the funeral is held.

The bond market's schedule is determined by the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA). Normal bond market hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern time Monday through Friday.

In 2026 and 2027, bond markets close for all 10 stock market holidays, in addition to Indigenous Peoples Day (formerly known as Columbus Day) in October and Veterans Day in November.

The bond market also closes early at 2 p.m. on the following days:

Thursday before Good Friday (Maundy Thursday)

Friday after Thanksgiving (Black Friday)

Is the stock market closed on the Friday after Thanksgiving?

The stock market is open on the Friday after Thanksgiving, but its trading session closes early at 1 p.m. Eastern time. It's one of two or three days annually that the stock market closes before 4 p.m.

Yes. Unlike the stock and bond markets, the crypto market doesn't observe a holiday schedule because cryptocurrency trades through a decentralized network of computers instead of through central exchanges. You can trade cryptocurrency 24/7/365.

Veterans Day isn't a stock market holiday, as both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are open for regular hours. However, the bond market does close in observance of Veterans Day.

articles.title: Nvidia dispara 30% no pré-mercado após volta de Jensen Huang | G1
articles.standfirst: Contratos futuros do Nasdaq 100 avançavam 6,53% após a fabricante de chips anunciar o retorno de seu CEO; papéis da empresa tiveram forte reação após uma semana de perdas.
articles.summary: Contratos futuros do Nasdaq 100 avançavam 6,53% após a fabricante de chips anunciar o retorno de seu CEO; papéis da empresa tiveram forte reação após uma semana de perdas.
articles.body:
As ações da Nvidia avançaram 29,5% nas negociações do pré-mercado nesta segunda-feira (23), após a empresa anunciar o retorno de Jensen Huang ao cargo de presidente-executivo (CEO). O movimento impulsionou os contratos futuros do Nasdaq 100, que dispararam 6,53%.

🔍 O que é o Nasdaq? É uma bolsa de valores dos EUA que reúne grandes empresas de tecnologia; seu índice Nasdaq 100 acompanha as 100 maiores companhias não financeiras listadas nela.

A reação ocorre depois de uma semana de fortes perdas para o setor de tecnologia. Na semana passada, as ações da Nvidia registraram a pior queda semanal desde 2008, em meio ao aumento das preocupações dos investidores com as perspectivas da inteligência artificial (IA).

O movimento também alcançou outros índices de Wall Street. Por volta das 9h02 (horário de Nova York), os contratos futuros do Dow Jones subiam 2,45%, enquanto os do S&P 500 avançavam 4,07%.

➡️ Os números são referentes às negociações antes da abertura oficial das bolsas americanas e, portanto, não representam o resultado definitivo do pregão.

Conselho da Nvidia volta atrás e reconduz executivo

A Nvidia anunciou nesta segunda-feira que Jensen Huang voltará imediatamente ao comando da companhia . A decisão foi aprovada por unanimidade pelo conselho de administração, após uma série de reuniões com o executivo.

A mudança representa uma reviravolta na posição da empresa, que havia descartado a possibilidade de recontratar Huang poucos dias antes

O executivo havia renunciado em 12 de novembro, após revelações sobre relacionamentos extraconjugais, incluindo um com Alice Huang, empresária suspeita pelas autoridades americanas de envolvimento em atividades de espionagem para a China.

Durante o afastamento, Colette Kress, diretora financeira da companhia, assumiu temporariamente o cargo de CEO. Ela continuará na função de CFO após o retorno de Huang.

Em comunicado, o presidente do conselho, Harvey Jones, afirmou que a empresa está satisfeita com a transparência do executivo e sua capacidade de voltar a liderar a fabricante de chips.

"O conselho acredita que Jensen é a pessoa certa para liderar a Nvidia e que seu retorno atende aos interesses de nossos acionistas, funcionários, parceiros e clientes", afirmou Jones.

A decisão também ocorreu após o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, defender publicamente a volta do empresário ao comando da Nvidia.

Na noite de domingo (22), Trump publicou nas redes sociais que a recontratação seria "a melhor coisa para a empresa e também para os Estados Unidos".

A Nvidia informou que consultou integrantes do alto escalão do governo americano antes de decidir pela reintegração. Segundo a companhia, o conselho recebeu informações de autoridades e concluiu que o retorno de Huang não representa riscos à segurança nacional.

A empresa também afirmou que uma investigação independente sobre possíveis tentativas de atuação de serviços de inteligência estrangeiros envolvendo o executivo continuará até sua conclusão.

Mercado de inteligência artificial estava sob pressão

A disparada das ações da Nvidia ocorre em um momento de cautela dos investidores com empresas ligadas à inteligência artificial.

Na semana passada, as ações de tecnologia sofreram fortes perdas diante de preocupações com os altos investimentos necessários para desenvolver a IA e dúvidas sobre a capacidade de transformar esses gastos em resultados financeiros.

A Nvidia ocupa uma posição central nesse mercado por comercializar chips utilizados no treinamento e na operação de sistemas de inteligência artificial. Por isso, o desempenho da companhia é acompanhado de perto por investidores interessados no futuro do setor.

A queda dos papéis da empresa na semana passada havia ampliado as preocupações sobre as perspectivas da IA. Com o anúncio da volta de Huang, a reação no pré-mercado indicava uma recuperação expressiva da confiança dos investidores na companhia.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante feira em Taiwan em junho de 2024 — Foto: REUTERS/Ann Wang/File Photo

articles.title: Fazenda de quase R$ 242 mi que abriga assentamento tem leilão suspenso | G1
articles.standfirst: Disputa judicial entre a família proprietária e a União se arrasta por quase 30 anos. Leilão seria para pagamento de dívidas da propriedade rural junto ao Banco do Brasil.
articles.summary: Disputa judicial entre a família proprietária e a União se arrasta por quase 30 anos. Leilão seria para pagamento de dívidas da propriedade rural junto ao Banco do Brasil.
articles.body:
Plantação na Fazenda Estreito da Ponte de Pedra, em Paraúna, Goiás: propriedade rural é alvo de disputa judicial entre a família e a União — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Max Lanio Gonçalves de Oliveira

O leilão de uma parte de uma fazenda de Goiás, avaliada em R$ 242 milhões, que abriga um assentamento do Movimento Sem-Terra (MST) com mais de 100 famílias foi suspenso pela Justiça em meio a uma disputa judicial que se arrasta por quase 30 anos. O leilão que seria realizado se refere a cerca de metade da área total e seria para quitar dívidas junto ao Banco do Brasil.

Localizada na região da divisa entre Paraúna , no oeste de Goiás, e Rio Verde , a Fazenda Estreito da Ponte de Pedra, de quase 5 mil hectares, foi ocupada pelos sem-terra em 1997. Ela pertencia à família Guindi, formada por imigrantes italianos que chegaram ao Brasil no início do século XX, como explica o advogado Max Lanio Gonçalves, que representa os proprietários. Hoje, a posse da fazenda é, oficialmente, do Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (Incra).

Max conta que, antes da ocupação, a fazenda sempre foi produtiva, com plantações de soja e tomate. Em função disso, pela legislação, cabe à família uma indenização a ser paga pela União, por conta da desapropriação indireta em benefício do assentamento rural.

"A Embrapa usava a fazenda como laboratório para testar novas novos grãos de soja. E eles produziram por muitos anos tomate para a Arisco", conta o advogado.

Produção de tomate na Fazenda Estreito da Ponte de Pedra, em Goiás — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Max Lanio Gonçalves de Oliveira

O imbróglio judicial que se arrasta por quase três décadas, que tramita atualmente no Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ), se refere à divergência do valor que a União quer pagar de indenização e o que a família afirma ser o justo. Segundo o advogado, a União fixou o valor de R$ 10 milhões para os proprietários, mas a fazenda vale pelo menos cerca de 50 vezes esse valor.

"Nós estamos defendendo no STJ que o imóvel vale R$ 510 milhões. O imóvel todo, só a terra nua. Fora as benfeitorias", explicou Max.

Paralelamente ao processo no STJ, existem ações judiciais de credores da fazenda, cobrando o pagamento de dívidas antigas. Entre esses credores está o Banco do Brasil.

"Vários desses créditos eram do Banco do Brasil. Até hoje, o Banco do Brasil é o principal fomentador do agronegócio (no país). Mas naquela época ele era praticamente o único", observou Max.

Ao suspender o leilão, que aconteceria no dia 16, a juíza Wanderlina Lima de Morais Tassi, da Vara das Fazendas Públicas de Paraúna, afirmou que, diante das controvérsias relacionadas ao imóvel e à intervenção de entes públicos federais trazida pelo proprietário, a decisão era necessária para evitar que o próprio leilão fosse anulado depois de realizado.

"A extensão das alegações trazidas quanto à ocupação do bem, individualização das matrículas e situação fática da posse demanda análise serena e prévia manifestação dos exequentes federais", afirmou a magistrada.

Os exequentes aos quais a juíza se refere são o Banco do Brasil e a União, autores da ação.

O g1 procurou o Banco do Brasil e a Procuradoria da República em Goiás, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Silo e armazém de soja na Fazenda Estreito da Ponte de Pedra, em Goiás, que foi ocupada por um assentamento rural em 1997 — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Max Lanio Gonçalves de Oliveira

Ao g1 , o advogado Max afirmou que a expectativa da família, em relação a todo o imbróglio judicial, não é retomar o imóvel e retirar as famílias assentadas, mas receber um valor justo de indenização.

"A despeito da da ilegalidade cometida para tirar a propriedade dos meus clientes, o assentamento Serra da Ponte de Pedra deu certo porque eles realmente produzem. Eu não sei quais tipos de cultura, mas eu acho que eles produzem até soja lá também", afirmou.

No entanto, como o imóvel já era produtivo antes da chegada dos sem-terra, os antigos proprietários tentam obter a devida reparação pelas suas perdas.

"Esse processo talvez seja um dos casos de maior injustiça de desapropriação do Brasil. (...) Vai fazer vai fazer 30 anos que eles estão sem a posse, sem a produtividade, sem a indenização e com todas as dívidas", destacou o advogado.

Pela decisão do TJGO, a União e o Banco do Brasil deverão se manifestar à Justiça sobre as pendências para a realização do leilão da metade da fazenda em até 15 dias.

Em relação ao processo principal, que abrange o imóvel como um todo, o STJ determinou à União, há cerca de dois meses, o pagamento da indenização. Mas a divergência sobre o valor ainda persiste e, por isso, não há prazo o caso ter um desfecho. "Estamos pedindo que seja paga pelo menos uma indenização mais consentânea com a realidade, que seja possível, inclusive, pagar as dívidas", disse o advogado.

articles.title: Batata na Lua: experimento mostra que cultivo em solo lunar é possível | G1
articles.standfirst: Cientistas conseguiram cultivar batatas nutritivas e seguras para consumo em solo lunar simulado, com o objetivo de alimentar astronautas que possam trabalhar em bases na superfície da Lua no futuro.
articles.summary: Usando solo lunar simulado e matéria orgânica, cientistas cultivaram batatas nutritivas que podem garantir a alimentação de astronautas em futuras bases na Lua.
articles.body:
Batatas cultivadas em solo que simula as condições da Lua em laboratório da Universidade Estadual do Oregon — Foto: Sean Nealon/Universidade Estadual do Oregon/Divulgação via REUTERS

A batata é uma das culturas mais importantes do planeta e fonte de amido, vitaminas, minerais e fibras. Em breve, ela poderá ganhar importância também na Lua.

Cientistas conseguiram cultivar batatas nutritivas e seguras para consumo em solo lunar simulado, com o objetivo de alimentar astronautas que possam trabalhar em bases na superfície da Lua no futuro.

Os pesquisadores adicionaram material orgânico ao simulador lunar e descobriram que, em quantidade suficiente, ele permite que as batatas cresçam tão bem quanto no solo terrestre.

A pesquisa, apoiada pela Nasa , envolveu uma variedade chamada Modoc, uma batata de maturação precoce com casca vermelha e polpa branca.

Estados Unidos e China pretendem enviar astronautas à superfície lunar nos próximos anos e planejam instalar bases de longo prazo na Lua. Produzir alimentos no local é considerado vital para sustentar as pessoas que trabalharão nessas bases, já que transportar da Terra toda a comida necessária seria impraticável.

“As batatas fornecem mais calorias por unidade de área do que muitas outras culturas”, disse o biólogo vegetal Aymeric Goyer, da Universidade Estadual do Oregon, que liderou o estudo publicado nesta quinta-feira na revista npj Microgravity.

“Elas são nutritivas — fornecem mais potássio do que uma banana, são ricas em vitamina C, contêm boas proteínas — e têm um alto índice de saciedade.”

Isso significa que as batatas promovem uma sensação de saciedade, como os fãs de batatas fritas já sabem.

O material que cobre a superfície da Lua é chamado, mais precisamente, de regolito lunar . Trata-se basicamente de rocha triturada e poeira , muitas vezes afiadas e semelhantes ao vidro , formadas ao longo de bilhões de anos por impactos de meteoritos. Ao contrário do solo terrestre, o regolito não contém material orgânico.

Os pesquisadores adicionaram ao regolito simulado diferentes quantidades de vermicomposto, uma substância rica em nutrientes produzida pela decomposição de resíduos orgânicos por minhocas.

“O regolito lunar não contém nitrogênio, portanto, nenhuma cultura cresceria sem essa suplementação”, disse Goyer.

Batatas plantadas no regolito sem vermicomposto quase não desenvolveram raízes nem produziram tubérculos.

As plantas desenvolveram algumas raízes e tubérculos em uma mistura com apenas 5% de vermicomposto e 95% de regolito.

Com 30% de vermicomposto, o rendimento foi igual ao das batatas cultivadas nas mesmas condições em solo terrestre , especificamente em Hermiston, no Oregon, região conhecida pelos altos rendimentos da cultura.

Os pesquisadores cultivaram as batatas em uma estufa, sob luz solar e artificial, com temperatura de 22°C durante o dia e 18°C à noite.

“Infelizmente, ainda não as provamos. Usamos o que colhemos para análises de laboratório”, declarou Goyer.

As plantas do estudo foram cultivadas em vasos pequenos. Por isso, as batatas produzidas também eram pequenas, geralmente com menos de 10 gramas, mesmo quando cultivadas em solo terrestre.

“Estamos trabalhando em um segundo estudo, no qual apresentaremos os resultados do crescimento de batatas cultivadas em vasos maiores. Nesse caso, obtivemos batatas do tamanho que você normalmente vê nas lojas”, disse Goyer.

articles.title: CVM suspende registro do BRB e banco para de negociar na bolsa | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (23) e atinge outras quatro companhias de capital aberto. BRB não divulga relatórios há um ano, por conta da crise com o Banco Master.
articles.summary: A CVM suspendeu o registro do BRB como companhia aberta devido a relatórios pendentes há mais de um ano, impedindo o banco de negociar suas ações na bolsa.
articles.body:
Sede do Banco de Brasília (BRB) — Foto: TV Globo

A Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) suspendeu nesta segunda-feira (23) o registro do Banco de Brasília (BRB) como companhia aberta.

Com isso, e até regularizar o registro, o BRB fica impedido de negociar ações em bolsa , entre outras restrições.

➡️ O motivo: como companhia aberta, o BRB tem a obrigação legal de divulgar balanços trimestrais – o que não acontece há um ano , segundo a própria CVM.

Entre as negociações fraudulentas, estava a tentativa do BRB de comprar o Master, entre 2024 e 2025 ( veja detalhes abaixo ).

O BRB negocia na B3 com os "tickers" (identificadores) BSLI3 e BSLI4 , para ações ordinárias e preferenciais , respectivamente. Na sexta-feira (19), as ações eram negociadas a R$ 1,89 e R$ 1,95, respectivamente.

"A SEP lembra que, enquanto o registro estiver suspenso, as companhias não podem ter os valores mobiliários por elas emitidos admitidos à negociação em mercados regulamentados, quais sejam: balcão organizado, bolsa ou balcão não organizado", explica a CVM no comunicado.

O g1 pediu posicionamento ao BRB e ao governo do DF – acionista controlador do banco – e aguarda retorno.

A atual crise do BRB está ligada às negociações e operações realizadas com o Banco Master .

Em março de 2025, o banco público anunciou a intenção de comprar parte da instituição privada .

A operação previa a compra de 49% das ações ordinárias e 100% das ações preferenciais do Master, após autorização aprovada pela Câmara Legislativa do DF.

Em novembro do mesmo ano, o Banco Master passou a ser alvo da Operação Compliance Zero , da Polícia Federal, que investiga um esquema de fraudes financeiras.

As investigações avançaram e passaram a analisar também negócios realizados entre BRB e Master.

O banco distrital injetou R$ 16,7 bilhões no Master. Segundo a Polícia Federal, pelo menos R$ 12,2 bilhões dessas operações apresentam indícios de irregularidades .

Em abril deste ano, uma nova fase da investigação levou à prisão do ex-presidente do BRB Paulo Henrique Costa .

A PF afirma que ele teria permitido negócios com o Master sem lastro e sem seguir práticas adequadas de governança.

Além do BRB, outras quatro firmas também tiveram o registro suspenso nesta segunda:

Ambipar Participações e Empreendimentos S.A.

Refinaria de Petróleos de Manguinhos S.A.

Essas quatro firmas já estão em recuperação judicial . Da lista, apenas o BRB opera sem o mecanismo de renegociação de dívidas.

articles.title: Controle da inflação é prioridade do Banco Central, diz Galípolo | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do BC também afirmou que é possível preservar programas sociais e rever regras fiscais que pressionem a inflação.
articles.summary: Presidente do BC também afirmou que é possível preservar programas sociais e rever regras fiscais que pressionem a inflação.
articles.body:
O presidente do Banco Central (BC), Gabriel Galípolo, afirmou nesta segunda-feira (23) que a prioridade da instituição é o controle da inflação.

"Tentamos muito cumprir o nosso mandato, que é de estabilidade de preços, perseguindo também os mandatos de menor relevância. [...] Mas está muito claro que, se só couber um, o mandato é de estabilidade de preços. Esse é o nosso mandato principal", afirmou Galípolo em evento promovido pelo Itaú.

Na prática, isso significa que o BC pode manter ou elevar os juros básicos do país (Selic) caso considere necessário para conter a inflação e levá-la à meta.

A afirmação vem duas semanas antes da última reunião do Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) do ano, quando o colegiado vai definir a Selic e poderá trazer novos sinais sobre o futuro da taxa , em meio às indicações de desaceleração da economia e de inflação acima da meta.

Segundo Galípolo, a recuperação do poder de compra nos últimos anos, por meio do reajuste do salário mínimo e de programas de recomposição de renda, ajudou a aliviar parte do desconforto da população com o nível dos preços.

Ele ponderou, porém, que esse processo de recuperação da renda também pode estimular a demanda e pressionar a inflação, principalmente em uma economia próxima do pleno emprego.

Para o presidente do BC, isso não significa que o governo precise abandonar medidas de recomposição de renda ou programas de proteção social. Segundo Galípolo, é possível preservar essas políticas e, ao mesmo tempo, rever regras que fazem determinadas despesas crescerem junto com a arrecadação.

"É possível preservar programas, benefícios e as pessoas que precisam disso e, simultaneamente, revisitar processos e gatilhos que temos, e que podem sugerir uma trajetória mais harmoniosa e com menos tensão entre as políticas econômicas", disse.

Galípolo afirmou ainda que há espaço para conciliar as demandas sociais escolhidas nas urnas com uma trajetória das contas públicas que gere menos pressão sobre a política monetária. Segundo ele, esse ajuste pode ser feito sem necessariamente promover cortes nominais nas despesas de um ano para outro.

Presidente do BC, Gabriel Galípolo — Foto: CLÁUDIO REIS/ENQUADRAR/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Medidas para conter endividamento das famílias

O presidente do BC também disse que a instituição continua estudando medidas para evitar o endividamento excessivo das famílias e aumentar a transparência nas ofertas de crédito.

A instituição anunciou, em outubro, novas regras para proteger consumidores contra ofertas de crédito que possam agravar situações de endividamento. A partir de 31 de março de 2027, clientes em situação de maior vulnerabilidade financeira ou risco de endividamento excessivo só poderão receber ofertas ativas de crédito mediante autorização prévia, específica e inequívoca.

Nesses casos, as ofertas deverão ter como objetivo melhorar as condições financeiras do cliente, como em renegociações ou portabilidade, sem a liberação de novos recursos.

Segundo Galípolo, o endividamento das famílias foi agravado nos últimos anos por uma série de fatores, desde os efeitos da pandemia de Covid-19 até a maior inclusão bancária dos consumidores.

"O que estamos tentando fazer é conseguir com que as pessoas tenham mais consciência sobre o que estão contratando, que tipo de custo ela vai incorrer a partir disso. A ideia é entender como a gente consegue dar mais visibilidade e ajudar as instituições também na concessão de crédito", disse.

articles.title: Mercado financeiro eleva estimativa de inflação em 2026 e 2027 e projeta corte menor dos juros no ano que vem | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central, com base em pesquisa realizada, na semana passada, com mais de 100 instituições financeiras.
articles.summary: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central, com base em pesquisa realizada, na semana passada, com mais de 100 instituições financeiras.
articles.body:
Os analistas do mercado financeiro elevaram a estimativa de inflação em 2026 e 2027 e passaram a projetar corte menor de juros no ano que vem.

As informações fazem parte do "Boletim Focus", divulgado nesta segunda-feira (23) pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada na última semana com mais de 100 instituições financeiras.

➡️ Para 2026, a estimativa de inflação subiu de 5,11% para 5,15%;

➡️ Para 2027, a expectativa subiu de 5% para 5,12%;

➡️ Para 2028, a previsão continuou em 4%;

➡️ Para 2029, a estimativa permaneceu em 4%.

articles.title: Jim Beam won't resume distilling at flagship Kentucky distillery in 2027
articles.summary: Jim Beam said production at its Clermont, Kentucky. distillery will remain paused. The site will still host events, tours as well as other operations.
articles.body:
Jim Beam announced that it intends to keep production paused at its Kentucky distillery as the state's signature bourbon industry faces continuing headwinds.

Jim Beam said in a statement to the Louisville Courier-Journal, part of the USA TODAY Network, that it intends to keep production paused at its Clermont, Kentucky, distilling operation in 2027 and that the company will "reassess production needs" in the future.

"The James B. Beam Distilling Co. Clermont campus is an important part of our Kentucky operations and the homeplace of Jim Beam," the company said in the Nov. 16 statement. "We remain committed to investing in Jim Beam and enhancing our Clermont campus as a hospitality destination."

Visitor experiences including tours, tastings, and dining at The Kitchen Table restaurant will continue at the Clermont campus. Jim Beam said it is planning additional programming and event experiences for the site.

The company said that the Fred B. Noe craft distillery at the Clermont campus, where brands including Knob Creek , Little Book and Booker's are produced, will continue operations. Aging, warehousing, and bottling operations will also continue at the campus.

No layoffs are associated with the continued pause at the Clermont distillery, the Courier-Journal reported.

The production pause was first announced in December 2025. Suntory Global Spirits , Jim Beam's parent company, said at the time that the move would allow Jim Beam to invest in site enhancements at its main facility, the Courier-Journal reported.

Jim Beam products will continue to be made during the pause at the Booker Noe Plant in Boston, Kentucky, the company's largest facility, about 12 miles away in neighboring Nelson County.

Jack Daniel's owner rejected $15B buyout Sazerac isn't backing down

Global beverage alcohol data and insight firm IWSR noted in an October report that U.S. whiskey inventories are three times higher than expected yearly demand, adding that the sector has "acute oversupply issues."

Marten Lodewijks, IWSR managing director and president, said in the report that the U.S. whiskey market, along with Scotch and Japanese whisky, is polarizing by price tier with "specific bands within each whisky sub-category" seeing growth.

"In most cases that growth is concentrating at the premium end, while the mainstream and value tiers absorb the pain," Lodewijks said.

Jim Beam is not the first Kentucky distiller to pause production this year. Lux Row Distillers halted production at its Bardstown distillery and Limestone Branch Distillery in Lebanon, Kentucky.

articles.title: JK Group's fifth gen leader Abhishek Singhania ventures into real estate
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: One of India’s oldest business houses — the Singhania family-run JK Group — is venturing big time into real estate by using significant land
articles.body: NEW DELHI: One of India’s oldest business houses — the Singhania family-run JK Group — is venturing big time into real estate by using significant land parcels held by it in UP and other places. Deriving its name from founder Juggilal (J) Singhania and his son Kamlapat (K) Singhania, one branch of the JK Organisation family headed by Abhishek Singhania has ventured into real estate with an initial investment of Rs 965 crore on six hotel projects with 650 keys in five destinations to begin with. The overall topline will be over Rs 4,400 crore across residential, mixed-use and urban redevelopment segments.JK Cotton, which started a mill in Kanpur in 1921, was rechristened JK Urbanscapes in 2022 that’s headed by Abhishek whose grandfather Padmapat was one of Kamlapat’s three sons. “The family owns substantial land parcels across UP and some other states. In Kanpur alone, for instance, the mill site was spread over 50 acres. To begin with, we will develop six acres of the same in Kanpur that will see two hotels that will be managed by Taj Group, including a Taj and a Ginger; Taj residences (serviced by the hotel group) and other uses,” said JK Urbanscapes CMD Abhishek Singhania. The Kanpur Taj and Ginger are expected to open in 2030.Part of JK Organisation, JK Urbanscapes Developers Ltd (JKUDL) has tied up with Taj parent Indian Hotels Co Ltd (IHCL) and Minor Hotels. The sites identified are known for pilgrimage, leisure, heritage and urban markets in UP, Uttarakhand, Bihar, West Bengal and Haryana.“We do not plan to take debt for land (acquisition). The leverage will be essentially construction finance. We will fund through a mix of debts and internal accruals. We will infuse equity,” said Abhishek Singhania.JK Urbanscapes’ residential portfolio includes the ongoing 90-acre Emerald Gulistan plotted residential township in Kanpur. “In Gurugram, our Advait Senior Living project in partnership with Pioneer Urban comprises 164 residences with a dedicated focus on senior living within a purpose-planned residential community,” said Maneesh Mansingka, joint MD of JK Urbanscapes.The company’s hospitality portfolio include a 78-key hotel in Bodh Gaya; a 41-key Kamla Castle hotel in Mussoorie; a 70-key hotel in Darjeeling and a 200-key hotel and residences project in Dehradun.“We also exploring hotel developments in Rishikesh, Jaipur and Kota. Through partnerships with established hospitality operators, including IHCL and Minor Hotels under its Anantara brand, we aim to combine hospitality expertise with a development approach shaped by the character and demand drivers of each location,” Mansingka added.Abhishek had also founded JK Tech (formerly JK Technosoft Ltd) in 1994 where he is MD. His Jaykay Enterprises manufactures components and products for the defence and aerospace sectors. “Hospitality is seeing a big boom in India and we will be present in this area too,” he said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Oil prices fall as global market selloff weighs on sentiment; Gulf attacks limit losses
articles.summary: Oil prices declined on Monday as a selloff in global financial markets spread to commodities, with concerns over the artificial intelligence sector's
articles.body: Oil prices declined on Monday as a selloff in global financial markets spread to commodities, with concerns over the artificial intelligence sector's ability to drive economic growth weighing on investor sentiment. However, continued attacks on Gulf shipping amid the unresolved US-Israeli war against Iran limited the decline.Brent crude futures fell 28 cents, or 0.30%, to $92.29 a barrel by 0216 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.18%, to $83.26 a barrel.Both benchmarks extended their losing streaks, with Brent declining 4% and WTI falling 5% last week.The weakness in oil prices came as Asian equity markets opened lower on Monday, following a sharp selloff in global technology stocks. South Korea's tech-heavy market dropped 4%, while markets in China, Hong Kong and Australia also traded lower. In the US, the Nasdaq plunged 10% last week amid concerns over the outlook for AI-related investments."It’s momentum carrying (oil) down," said Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at Sydney-based XAnalysts.However, Sahdev cautioned that attacks on shipping could eventually put upward pressure on crude prices. "ballast (empty) vessels counts are building in crude while laden vessels are not. This risk to flows will start to price soon."The continuing conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran has kept concerns over energy supplies elevated. On Sunday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery. Multiple attacks on commercial shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz were also reported over the weekend.The Strait of Hormuz is a key global oil transit route, making any disruption to shipping in the region a potential risk to international crude supplies.Meanwhile, disagreements over fossil fuels continued at the global climate summit COP31 in Turkey. Talks collapsed on Sunday after participating nations failed to reach an agreement on including a reference to phasing out fossil fuels in the final text. It was the first such breakdown at the summit since 2009.Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing countries have maintained that fossil fuels will remain part of the global economy for the foreseeable future. Observers at the summit said these countries lobbied to keep references to fossil fuels out of the final document. The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) had also defended fossil fuel use at the summit.Meanwhile, OPEC and its allies, collectively known as OPEC+, are scheduled to hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their oil production policy for 2027. The group includes Russia and other major oil-producing nations.Foreign inflows support rupee, government bonds; oil prices and US yields in focusStrong foreign investment inflows are expected to support the Indian rupee and government bonds during the holiday-shortened week, with crude oil prices and US Treasury yields likely to remain key factors influencing domestic markets.The Indian rupee closed at 92.67 against the US dollar on Friday, strengthening past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. The currency gained 1.7% during the week.Government bonds also recorded gains, with the benchmark 10-year bond yield declining 12 basis points last week to 7.1868%. It marked the yield's third weekly decline in four weeks. Traders expect the benchmark yield to trade in the range of 7.10% to 7.25% this week. Bond prices move inversely to yields.The improvement in domestic financial markets has been supported by a shift in global investment flows away from AI-related stocks amid a deepening selloff in technology shares. India's relatively insulated equity markets have attracted foreign investment worth a record $12 billion, supporting the rupee and increasing demand for fixed-income assets.The shift has also prompted investors to unwind bearish positions on the rupee. Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian bonds in November after three consecutive months of selling, purchasing nearly $1.2 billion worth of bonds in the first three weeks of the month.Lower crude oil prices and declining US Treasury yields have further supported the domestic market, offsetting concerns over a potentially more hawkish stance by the US Federal Reserve."Indian assets have benefited from a broader rotation away from AI-related exposures, alongside lower oil prices, which helped improve the macro backdrop and supported sentiment. These will be important drivers going forward also," said Shamaila Khan, head of fixed income for emerging markets and Asia-Pacific at UBS Asset Management.A trader at a private bank said continued foreign investment inflows could support the rupee in the coming days. Market participants will also watch for signs of intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), particularly the levels at which it may step in to replenish its foreign exchange reserves.Norbert Ling, head of fixed income portfolio management for Asia-Pacific at Invesco, said Indian government bonds were benefiting from attractive carry, resilient domestic fundamentals and the possibility of inclusion in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index.However, market participants remain cautious about the outlook, with inflation, crude oil prices and central bank decisions likely to influence investor sentiment.Attention will turn to US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data due on Wednesday, followed by the RBI's monetary policy decision on December 4 and the US Federal Reserve's meeting on December 9.Markets expect both central banks to raise interest rates by 25 basis points. However, an increase in expectations of a larger rate hike by the Fed could put pressure on Indian financial assets.Ling cautioned that inflation remained above the RBI's tolerance band and that crude oil prices, despite their recent decline, remained vulnerable to renewed geopolitical tensions."The INR has stabilized and strengthened amid improving equity inflows, partly reflecting a rotation away from AI-related stocks, but the durability of this trend remains uncertain."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Bisleri water samples declared 'unsafe' by food regulator; company responds
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Packaged drinking water major Bisleri International Pvt Ltd on Monday maintained that its products remain safe for consumption, after the Food
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Packaged drinking water major Bisleri International Pvt Ltd on Monday maintained that its products remain safe for consumption, after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against the company over a sample of its packaged drinking water declared unsafe.“Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process and will continue to cooperate with FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process. A trusted brand for years, Bisleri remains safe for consumption,” the company said.In a detailed media statement, Bisleri said the regulatory matter concerned a single batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network. The company also said it had not received any official notice from the food regulator.“We are aware of recent media reports that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued a notice to Bisleri. The matter dates back approximately 14 months, to a batch produced in September 2025 at Bisleri’s Goa manufacturing facility, one of 143 plants in our network,” the statement said.Bisleri disputes laboratory findingsAccording to the company, the FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. Initial tests found that five samples met all applicable standards, while the sixth recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.Following an appeal by Bisleri on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for further testing. The laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit but separately detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).Bisleri said the difference between the test results raised questions that required clarification. It subsequently arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which also found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit.The company said it submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI's Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.“We submitted the independent test results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office with a formal letter dated 2 February 2026. We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed. To date, Bisleri has received no notice by email or in hard copy and has been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI’s website,” the company said.What FSSAI said about the sampleThe company's statement followed the FSSAI's announcement that it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri over the packaged drinking water sample.In a social media post, the regulator said a sample of “Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)” collected from the company's premises did not comply with prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.After Bisleri appealed against the findings, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory, which also declared it unsafe after detecting PAHs, the FSSAI said. The regulator said the findings established violations relating to unsafe food under the law, leading it to sanction prosecution against the company.Four other food businesses face prosecutionThe FSSAI has also sanctioned prosecution against four other food businesses: Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.Separately, it suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store over non-compliance with food safety rules. The regulator also ordered Asha Confectionery to recall its pre-packaged chocolate-filled cookies after they were found unsafe.FSSAI steps up enforcementThe action comes amid stepped-up enforcement by the FSSAI against food business operators and e-commerce companies during the current calendar year. The regulator has also intensified scrutiny of energy drink and alcoholic beverage manufacturers.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, India’s high-speed train project, achieves power milestone as 50-km Surat-Bilimora section is energised; Surat-Vapi operations deadline now stands at late 2027
articles.summary: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor: India’s first bullet train corridor has achieved yet another milestone.
articles.body: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor: India’s first bullet train corridor has achieved yet another milestone. The overhead electrical equipment that will supply power to trains on the Surat-Bilimora stretch of the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor has been successfully energised, the railway ministry announced on Saturday.The process will now move ahead in phases, with shorter stretches being energised one at a time.The Surat-Bilimora stretch covers around 50 km between the two stations, with the tracks running along an elevated viaduct. The route crosses four rivers by means of bridges and also includes a steel bridge spanning National Highway 53.The Surat-Vapi corridor is the first stretch of the bullet train or high-speed rail corridor that is expected to be operationalised in the second half of 2027.‘Energisation’ of India’s first bullet train corridor"Energisation will be carried out progressively in smaller sections, under the close supervision of technical teams to ensure safety and compliance with prescribed procedures," a railway ministry press statement said.Alongside the development, the ministry issued a public safety warning asking residents, commuters, construction personnel and others in areas near the corridor to stay away from overhead electrical equipment. It also cautioned against touching these installations or carrying out any unauthorised activity near the section.Officials clarified that switching on the power supply does not indicate that the stretch is ready for passenger train services. However, they described the milestone as an important step towards making the section operational.The ministry has recently pushed back the target for launching Bullet Train services on the 100-km Surat-Vapi stretch. The deadline, initially set for August 2027, has been moved to the final quarter of 2027."The section comprises both Up and Down lines on the elevated alignment and marks an important advancement towards further testing activities for the project," the ministry said.The ministry said the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor uses an advanced 2 × 25 kV overhead traction system, a sophisticated electrification technology deployed in high-speed rail networks around the world.Power for the system will be drawn from the national grid through 14 traction substations (TSS) positioned at strategic points along the 508-km route. "The electrification network comprises 14 strategically located traction substations (TSS) along the 508-km corridor. These substations will receive power from the national grid and supply it to the overhead traction system used by high-speed trains," the ministry said.A centralised control centre will oversee the entire electrical network, enabling the system to be monitored for safe and dependable operation.To reduce noise reaching nearby areas, the viaduct has been fitted with around 94,000 noise barriers, officials said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday announced that it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for Rs 15,510
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday announced that it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for Rs 15,510 crore at Rs 2,100 per share. The company will subsequently launch an open offer to acquire an additional 26% stake at Rs 2,301.40 per share, taking the total proposed investment to Rs 16,756 crore.The agreement has been signed between Tata Steel and SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd (SG Spectra), an entity associated with APL Apollo's promoter group, according to a company statement.The proposed transactions are subject to regulatory approvals, which Tata Steel expects to secure in the coming months. The company aims to complete the entire transaction within the financial year 2026-27 (FY27).The acquisition is expected to strengthen Tata Steel's presence in the downstream steel products segment, particularly steel tubes and colour-coated products. APL Apollo will serve as a platform for Tata Steel to expand its downstream operations and drive growth in these segments.Under the proposed arrangement, the combined entity, APL Apollo Tubes Pvt Ltd, aims to build a production capacity of up to 15.5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) by 2035. This will include 9 MTPA of steel tubes and 6.5 MTPA of colour-coated products.Tata Steel said the combination would help optimise capacity utilisation, unlock value, improve profitability and leverage the strengths of both companies.T V Narendran, CEO and managing director of Tata Steel, said: "We are very pleased to have entered into a comprehensive agreement with APL Apollo and the promoters as we create a downstream powerhouse for the future characterised by its inherent strengths of agility in the market, strong growth trajectory and benchmark capex-opex profile to serve the growing Indian market."This strategic move helps to consolidate the steel tubes and the colour coated business under Tata Steel's ownership while unlocking multiple synergies between the two companies. This will create value for all stakeholders with enhanced customer centricity, pan-India reach, and a full product portfolio. We look forward to working with our partners through this exciting journey."Tata Steel executive director and chief financial officer Koushik Chatterjee said the acquisition aligned with the company's strategy to expand its presence in value-added steel products through organic and inorganic growth.He said: "We have, over the last year, emphasised our strategic intent to grow aggressively in the value-added space and expand our downstream footprint both organically and inorganically. While we have multiple projects under construction in value-added segments like tin plate and hot-rolled, pickled and galvanised lines, APL Apollo presented a unique opportunity for us."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Chris Peverell, 40 años: "Dejé un restaurante con estrella Michelin para convertirme en electricista. Gano 20.000 euros menos, pero tengo más tiempo para mi familia"
articles.standfirst: Una decisión que le acabó cambiando la vida por completo
articles.summary: Una decisión que le acabó cambiando la vida por completo
articles.body: En la vida, en algunas ocasiones hay que tomar decisiones arriesgadas que pueden salir mal o bien. En este contexto, aparece la historia de Chris Peverell, camarero de 40 años que dejó su restaurante con estrella Michelin para ser electricista. Todos los entresijos de su decisión los recogió el periódico británico Mirror. Peverell afirmó ganar 20.000 euros menos, pero tener “más” tiempo para su familia. Peverell comenzó con 15 años en el pub de su barrio a trabajar y luego, estudió gestión hotelera. Tras ello, trabajó para el chef Tommy Banks en el restaurante de The Black Swan y como jefe de alimentos y bebidas en el Hotel Saltmoore de Whitby, donde supervisaba tres restaurantes, uno de ellos con estrella Michelin. Peverell tiene dos hijos (de siete y seis años) y está casado con Sophie. En declaraciones recogidas por Mirror afirmó lo siguiente al respecto: “Me gustaba mucho mi trabajo, pero en la vida las cosas cambian y hay que cambiar de rumbo. En 2019 le dije a mi esposa que cuando los niños vayan al colegio, no quería perderme los fines de semana ni nada más. Ese fue el detonante. Me di cuenta de que me estaba perdiendo demasiados momentos y hace aproximadamente un año me dije a mí mismo: “Lo voy a hacer”. En octubre de 2025 dejó la restauración y se preparó para ser electricista. Desde septiembre de este año trabaja para una empresa de Whitby, pero descarta abrir un negocio de este tipo: “He oído a otros compañeros decir que trabajar solo puede hacerme perder el tiempo libre que tanto anhelaba”. De ganar 45.000 libras a 27.000 al cambiar la hostelería por la electricidad es algo que ve así: “Es bajo, pero hay que prepararse, pero merecerá la pena. Antes trabajaba de miércoles a domingo, de 60 a 70 horas semanales, cubriendo el desayuno, el almuerzo y la cena. A veces terminaba a la 1 de la madrugada y tenía que estar de vuelta en el trabajo a las 6:30”. “Ahora trabajo de lunes a viernes, 40 horas a la semana. Desayuno con mi familia y llego a casa a tiempo para la cena . Es increíble cómo ha cambiado nuestra vida. Nunca habíamos pasado tanto tiempo juntos: de verdad no sé por qué tardé tanto en hacerlo. Incluso pude llevar a los niños al colegio por la mañana, algo que nunca había hecho antes, y es maravilloso”, sentenció.

The daily Bollinger Band levels are approximately Rs 1,50,266 (upper), Rs 1,37,247 (middle) and Rs 1,24,228 (lower). Gold is attempting to stabilise near the lower band, but the broader daily trend remains weak until it reclaims the middle band.Gold is showing an initial recovery near Rs 1,24,330 after a sharp and prolonged correction from the February-March highs above Rs 1,60,000. However, the daily chart continues to reflect a distinctly bearish broader structure, with prices trading significantly below the 20-day average near Rs 1,37,247.The Bollinger Bands are positioned around Rs 1,50,266 on the upside and Rs 1,24,228 on the downside, indicating that prices have approached the lower boundary following the latest sell-off. The sharp decline has also been accompanied by increased trading volume, suggesting heightened liquidation and volatility. Immediate support is placed around Rs 1,24,000-1,23,500, followed by Rs 1,20,000. The broader trend would require a sustained move above Rs 1,37,000 to indicate meaningful improvement. Overall, the immediate rebound may encourage short-covering and bargain hunting, but the broader technical structure remains weak. A sustained hold above Rs 1,24,000 is important for stabilisation, while a recovery above Rs 1,30,000 would provide stronger evidence that selling pressure is beginning to ease.Gold has staged a recovery after touching a 14-month low, with the latest rebound supported by renewed safe-haven demand amid a technology-led sell-off in global equity markets. Gold gained ~ 1.5% during Asian trading on Monday, while US gold futures advanced around 2.1%. Silver also recovered, rising approximately 0.8% to $41.59/oz.The rebound follows a significant correction in precious metals, during which gold and silver experienced substantial liquidation as investors reassessed the outlook for US monetary policy. However, the latest recovery needs to be viewed cautiously, as it is emerging against a backdrop of elevated yields, dollar strength and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening.The technology-led sell-off has become an important factor influencing precious-metal flows. Weakness in technology shares, particularly concerns surrounding elevated AI valuations and the sustainability of investment spending, has increased demand for defensive assets. Gold has consequently regained some of its safe-haven appeal after its recent decline. However, the relationship between equities and bullion remains complicated.During the earlier stages of the technology correction, investors liquidated profitable gold and silver positions to meet margin requirements and raise cash, contributing to the sharp decline in precious metals. The latest rebound suggests that some investors are returning to gold as portfolio protection, although a sustained recovery will depend on whether safe-haven demand can outweigh the pressure from higher interest rates.Federal Reserve expectations remain the principal macroeconomic headwind. Minutes from the October 27-28 FOMC meeting indicated that nearly all policymakers expected a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, while some officials favoured a larger move to contain persistent inflation. This reinforced the market’s increasingly hawkish interpretation of the Fed’s policy trajectory.Markets are now pricing approximately a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December, alongside a smaller probability of a 50-basis-point move. The possibility of further tightening extending into 2027 is also becoming an important consideration.Treasury yields and the dollar will therefore remain critical determinants of the next move. Stronger US economic activity and persistent inflation have supported expectations of further tightening, keeping financial conditions restrictive. The dollar has also remained relatively firm, making precious metals more expensive for international buyers.Any further rise in yields or dollar strength could restrict the current recovery, while a moderation in inflation expectations could provide room for a more sustained rebound. The important distinction for gold is whether the technology-led equity weakness generates a genuine shift towards defensive assets or merely another temporary episode of liquidity-driven trading.Silver faces additional challenges because of its exposure to industrial demand. Concerns over global growth, manufacturing activity and the outlook for Chinese consumption continue to weigh on sentiment. Unlike gold, silver’s recovery depends not only on investment flows and monetary-policy expectations but also on confidence in industrial applications, including electronics, solar energy and manufacturing.The recent decline in silver has therefore been more pronounced, reflecting both speculative unwinding and uncertainty over the industrial demand outlook. A sustained recovery in silver would require improving investment sentiment alongside stabilisation in expectations for global manufacturing activity.Attention now shifts towards the upcoming US PCE inflation report, which remains particularly important as the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure. A stronger reading could reinforce expectations of a December rate increase, push yields higher and restrict further gains in gold and silver.Conversely, softer inflation could moderate tightening expectations and provide additional support to precious metals. Overall, the latest rebound reflects bargain hunting and renewed safe-haven demand rather than a confirmed reversal of the broader bearish trend.Gold’s structural investment appeal remains supported by diversification demand and geopolitical uncertainty, but the immediate outlook will continue to depend on the interaction between technology-sector volatility, inflation, Treasury yields and the Federal Reserve’s policy trajectory.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Fidelity: Retirement balances dip amid market volatility, but workers keep saving
articles.summary: Average retirement balances with Fidelity Investments across IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s slipped modestly in the third quarter from the end of June,
articles.body:
Retirement savers have kept their heads down through 2026, contributing paycheck after paycheck to their retirement accounts, despite market volatility that has eroded balances.

Average retirement balances with Fidelity Investments across IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s slipped modestly in the third quarter from the end of June, but are still ahead of a year ago, according to a new report.

The average 401(k) account balance dipped 2% in the third quarter, but was up 5% from a year earlier. Individual retirement account (IRA) balances dropped 1%, and 403(b) accounts were down 2%.

Fidelity's average 401(k) balance was $152,500 at the end of September, down from $155,800 at the end of June, but still above the $141,000 at the end of March. The average IRA climbed to $142,261, an uptick from $131,400 in March.

"One of the most encouraging themes in this quarter's data is that retirement savers are staying focused on what they can control," Mike Shamrell, vice president of workplace thought leadership at Fidelity Investments, told Yahoo Finance.

"Even amid shifting markets, the vast majority of workers maintained or increased their savings rate," he added. "That type of consistency can be incredibly powerful over time and highlights a growing understanding that long-term retirement success is built through steady saving, not short-term market timing."

It's a tried-and-true strategy. Regular saving goes further when stocks slide and pays off when the market bounces back.

Average total savings rates, which include both employee and employer contributions, are 14.3% for 401(k) participants, down only slightly from last quarter. That amount includes an employee contribution rate of 9.6%, combined with an average employer contribution of 4.7%. Fidelity suggests a 15% savings rate.

Boomers and Gen X savers are pushing even harder to build a stash with average savings rates of 17.3% and 15.7%, respectively. Millennials with average 401(k) balances that have increased 17% year over year, are grinding it out as well.

The 401(k) data is based on Fidelity's 27,722 defined-contribution plans at various companies across the country, covering 26.2 million participants.

"Many workers are not just staying invested; they're continuing to make retirement saving a financial priority," Shamrell said. "Workplace retirement plans with features like automatic enrollment and employer contributions help people keep moving forward, even during periods of market uncertainty."

articles.title: India, Vietnam to lead Asia-Pacific growth in 2027 as China slows: S&P
articles.summary: India's economy is expected to grow by 7 per cent in both the current and the next financial years, keeping the country among the fastest-growing
articles.body: India's economy is expected to grow by 7 per cent in both the current and the next financial years, keeping the country among the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027, according to S&P Global Ratings.In its Economic Outlook for Asia-Pacific, released on Monday, the rating agency said India and Vietnam were likely to lead regional growth next year, with Vietnam's economy projected to expand by 7.5 per cent.China's growth, meanwhile, is expected to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent in 2026.S&P said India's expansion during the June and September quarters was supported by strong goods exports, public-sector investment and household consumption, with the latter benefiting from buoyant credit growth."We expect Vietnam and India to be the region's fastest-growing economies in 2027," the agency said.India's export performance has benefited from higher commodity prices, trade diversification and its growing integration into global supply chains. S&P said the strength was particularly visible in electronic and engineering goods, as well as chemicals.El Nino, rising costs pose inflation risksDespite the strong growth outlook, S&P expects India's growth-inflation mix to become less favourable in the second half of the current financial year, as higher input costs are increasingly passed on to consumers.It flagged uneven monsoon conditions, deficient summer rainfall and lower reservoir levels as factors that could weigh on current agricultural output and the upcoming winter crop. Persistent El Nino conditions are also expected to put pressure on food prices across Asia-Pacific, particularly in India.The agency expects inflation in India to average 5.3 per cent in the financial year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside.Retail inflation stood at 6.1 per cent in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's tolerance band of 2-6 per cent.S&P anticipates a further 25-basis-point policy rate hike by the RBI in December, followed by another increase in early 2027. It expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the financial year ending March 2028.India is scheduled to release its official GDP growth data for the July-September quarter on November 30.The RBI had projected 7.2 per cent growth for the quarter, while the Finance Ministry's Monthly Economic Review estimated it at 7.35 per cent.Asia-Pacific growth to moderate, China remains weak spotAt the regional level, S&P expects Asia-Pacific economic growth to ease to 4.4 per cent in 2027 from 4.8 per cent in 2026. It identified high energy prices as the biggest macroeconomic headwind and the global expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure as the largest growth tailwind, although both forces are expected to moderate somewhat next year.The agency expects exports to remain strong, largely driven by shipments of AI-related technology, while domestic demand is likely to stay broadly resilient outside China.However, it warned that technology export growth could peak in the coming quarters because of challenging base effects and a possible slowdown in AI infrastructure investment in the US and other markets.China is expected to remain a weak spot in the regional outlook, with S&P projecting its growth to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent this year.The agency cited weak domestic demand, a prolonged downturn in the housing sector and subdued consumption and investment.It also said the likelihood of significant fresh policy stimulus in China was limited, given that the country's 2026 growth target of 4.5 per cent was within reach.S&P identified three major risks to the regional outlook: a significant slowdown in global AI-related spending, persistently high energy prices and a sharper increase in global interest rates.While consumer inflation across Asia-Pacific is expected to moderate in 2027 as the impact of higher energy prices eases, the agency cautioned that prolonged high energy costs could push inflation and interest rates higher.Stronger pressure from US interest rates could also trigger capital outflows and currency depreciation in some economies.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Billionaire Bill Ackman sounds the alarm on Wall Street's next big risk
articles.summary: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman sends a fresh warning out on the Federal Reserve.
articles.body:
Billionaire investor Bill Ackman thinks the Federal Reserve is about to make a big mistake.

In his view, the central bank is trying too hard to fix its long-running mistake on inflation.

"I think the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. Financial conditions have tightened massively. For example, SpaceX ( SPCX ), an investment-grade company, just raised secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate versus below 6% for its unsecured bond offering at the time of its IPO. The cost of equity capital has also increased materially with the recent substantial decline in the stock market," the CEO of Pershing Square said in a new X post .

He added, "The Fed's 2% inflation ambition is misguided. Geopolitical risk, the required investment in global military spending, deglobalization and tariffs, and massive AI infrastructure and related energy investment are features of the world that did not exist when the 2% target was set. 3% inflation is a more realistic ambition in the new world. The Fed will put the U.S. and the world in recession if it continues to raise rates in a failed attempt to drive inflation to 2%."

Of course, Ackman is talking his book. Lower interest rates would benefit the stock market and his many stock holdings, such as Microsoft and Netflix.

Moreover, it's hard to argue that inflation hasn't worsened, or that need to act more aggressively to bring it under contr' it under control.

The inflation picture has deteriorated in recent months, with the October Consumer Price Index (CPI) showing prices rising 0.4% month over month, following a 0.6% increase in September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose another 0.3%, marking the third consecutive month at that pace and suggesting underlying price pressures remain stubborn.

The Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, was up 3.6% year over year in September. Core PCE clocked in at 3.1% — both well above the Fed's 2% target.

Inflation doesn't appear to be cooling fast enough, raising the possibility that interest rates may need to stay higher for longer or even move higher again.

The Fed lifted interest rates in September after sticky inflation readings , fueled in part by the AI boom and rising energy costs , forced central bankers back into tightening mode. The rate hike marked the central bank's first increase since July 2023.

At its late-October meeting, the Fed held steady, which many now see as a mistake.

"If you break out the categories of where the inflation is, it's kind of in the wrong, more disturbingly persistent categories like services, healthcare, a series of things that really can't be coming from tariffs or oil prices," Chicago Federal Reserve president Austan Goolsbee said at Yahoo Finance's Invest earlier this month . "I think it's worth being sober-minded at a moment like this that we're inching our way into a territory that's historically a tough spot for any central bank to try to get rid of that inflation. We'd do well to try to prevent it from getting worse."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Social Security payments go out Nov. 25. Who gets paid?
articles.summary: Social Security payments go out Nov. 25 for recipients born between the 21st and 31st. See who gets paid and how the schedule works.
articles.body:
The third and final round of November Social Security payments is set to go out this week.

Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st of any month are scheduled to receive their monthly benefit on Wednesday, Nov. 25, according to the Social Security Administration's payment calendar.

Here's what to know about this week's payment and the remaining Social Security and SSI payment dates for 2026.

Who gets their Social Security payment this week?

Social Security recipients with birthdays between the 21st and 31st of any month are set to receive their November payment on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

It's the third and final round of November payments under the regular Social Security schedule .

For most recipients, when your Social Security payment arrives depends on your birthday:

Born between the 1st and 10th: Your payment typically arrives on the second Wednesday of the month.

Born between the 11th and 20th: Your payment typically arrives on the third Wednesday.

Born between the 21st and 31st: Your payment typically arrives on the fourth Wednesday.

If you started receiving Social Security benefits before May 1997, you generally get your payment on the third day of the month. If that date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the payment schedule may shift.

If you receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, you generally get your Social Security payment on the third of the month and your SSI payment on the first.

Social Security recipients will get a 3.6% COLA in 2027

Recipients will also get a boost to their benefits next year.

Social Security's cost-of-living adjustment will be 3.6% in 2027, up from 2.8% in 2026.

The annual adjustment is designed to help benefits keep pace with inflation. But many older Americans say those increases haven't been enough to keep up with rising expenses, according to AARP.

When are the remaining SSI payments for 2026?

SSI payments typically go out on the first day of the month. If the first falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the payment is generally sent on the previous business day.

articles.title: Petrol, diesel prices rose just 7% in India in four years versus 50-70% globally, says Hardeep Puri; but India’s oil and gas import bill has jumped 60% to $16 billion in October 2026 as Brent nearly doubled
articles.summary: India has seen its petrol and diesel prices rise, but the government has said that the hike has much less compared to other major global economies.
articles.body: India has seen its petrol and diesel prices rise, but the government has said that the hike has much less compared to other major global economies.Oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Sunday that petrol and diesel prices in India had risen by just 7% over a four-year reference period, significantly less than the increase of 50-70% recorded in other parts of the world.He credited the relatively limited rise to three reductions in central excise duty and the role of oil marketing companies in absorbing losses instead of passing the entire burden on to consumers.Government says oil price rise containedDetailing the Centre’s efforts to keep fuel prices in check, Puri said excise duty had been cut on three occasions since November 2021. He maintained that, over the four-year period under consideration, fuel prices in India had actually declined.“India is a unique case globally….In fact, if you look at a four-year reference period, prices in India have actually decreased. Meanwhile, elsewhere in the world, petrol and diesel prices surged by 50–70%, whereas in India, they increased by only 7%,” Puri said.He said the divergence between domestic and international fuel price movements was the result of both the Centre’s three excise duty cuts and the actions of oil marketing companies. According to the minister, these companies took on substantial financial losses rather than transferring the full impact to customers.“This is because the central government reduced excise duty three times, and our oil marketing companies such as BPCL, IOCL, and HPCL acted as responsible corporate citizens. They absorbed significant losses and operated at a deficit,” he said.Puri acknowledged that international conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty continued to pose challenges. He expressed hope that tensions would eventually ease, paving the way for a decline in crude oil prices.“I am not speaking in the past tense, as if the matter is entirely behind us; we still face challenges. The war between Russia and Ukraine is ongoing, and there are also tensions involving Iran, the US, and Israel. We hope that these tensions subside and that the price of crude oil decreases,” he said.India’s oil bill balloonsMeanwhile, India’s net expenditure on oil and gas imports climbed 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October, driven by a sharp rise in crude oil prices. Brent crude averaged $124.77 a barrel during the month, nearly twice its level a year earlier, according to data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), which functions under the oil ministry.The net import bill had stood at $10 billion in October 2025. Spending on crude oil imports alone increased to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion a year earlier, although the volume of imports grew by just 11% to 23.3 million tonnes. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports accounted for $1.3 billion, while exports of petroleum products generated $6.3 billion.Brent crude had averaged $116.77 a barrel in September, compared with $64.75 in October 2025. The average price of India’s crude oil basket also rose sharply, reaching $119.91 a barrel in October against $65.08 in the corresponding month last year.For the April-October period, India’s net oil and gas import bill expanded to $97.7 billion from $70.3 billion a year earlier. Although crude oil import volumes increased by only 2.7%, the expenditure on these imports surged to $111 billion, compared with $72.3 billion in the year-ago period.Meanwhile, domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumption contracted by 12.3% in October and 15.1% during April-October. PPAC data showed that the number of active domestic LPG consumers declined to 32.6 crore as of November 1, from 33.4 crore on April 1.Direct imports of LPG by private players also dropped sharply, falling 83.8% in October and 97.3% over the first seven months of the financial year. Sales of packed domestic LPG by state-owned companies declined 11.8% in October, while bulk LPG sales recorded a steeper contraction of 49.1%. In contrast, auto LPG sales increased by 23.9%.India’s imports of petroleum products contracted 41.2% in October, taking the decline for the current financial year so far to 49.3%. articles.body: Malaysian budget carrier AirAsia reported a net loss of 381.3 million ringgit ($92.5 million) for the third quarter, as high jet fuel prices and foreign exchange losses continued to pressure its finances, even as the airline reduced its losses from the previous quarter.The loss for the three months ended September 30 was less than half the 830.5 million ringgit loss recorded in the second quarter. The loss attributable to equity holders stood at 175 million ringgit.Revenue, however, declined 8.4% to 4.66 billion ringgit from 5.09 billion ringgit in the preceding quarter, as the airline cut capacity by 12% amid efforts to rationalise its fleet. Nearly a third of its 234 aircraft, or about 31%, remained grounded at the end of September.AirAsia, Southeast Asia's largest budget carrier, has described the period as its most difficult financial stretch since the pandemic. The Iran war drove up jet fuel prices, adding to the cost pressures facing the airline.The carrier also took a 141.9 million ringgit net foreign exchange hit as local currencies weakened against the US dollar. It did not declare a dividend.The airline did not provide year-on-year comparisons, citing accounting changes following its January acquisition of the aviation business of affiliate Capital A.AirAsia said it was cautiously optimistic about the coming months, with peak-season travel and fleet modernisation expected to improve its resilience as it enters 2027. The airline is increasing capacity on high-demand domestic and international routes to tap year-end travel.But cost pressures are expected to persist. AirAsia said fourth-quarter fuel expenses would likely remain above third-quarter levels, despite a recent moderation in jet fuel prices.Its balance sheet remains under strain. Cash and bank balances stood at 905.3 million ringgit at the end of September, down from 954 million ringgit in June, while current liabilities rose to 19.2 billion ringgit from 18.4 billion ringgit.The airline, which holds about 60% of Malaysia's domestic aviation market and employs around 26,000 people, has seen its stock lose roughly 75% of its value this year.AirAsia is seeking to raise as much as $1 billion through international debt markets, alongside 700 million ringgit in local credit facilities, mainly to refinance existing borrowings.The airline gave no fresh timeline on Monday, saying it remained in active discussions with local and international financial institutions and was pursuing measures to improve liquidity.Money habits form by age 7.
