articles.title: Walmart’s turkey dinner deal draws a rush of orders
articles.summary: Walmart's $35 holiday meal basket is already one of the most affordable in retail, but a limited-time $10 promotion is driving even stronger sales.
articles.body:
Walmart's $35 holiday meal basket is one of the most affordable Thanksgiving combos in retail.

Shoppers are also stacking the deal with a $10-off promotion that is driving higher sales.

Workers say fulfilling the orders is chaotic, but the savings offer real relief from high prices.

Walmart shoppers have been loading up on turkey dinner supplies.

With a week to go before Thanksgiving, CEO John Furner said Thursday that the holiday is off to a brisk start this year.

"This month we've sold a million more turkeys than we did a year ago," he said. "The customer response is strong," he said.

Walmart's deal is already one of the most affordable Thanksgiving baskets available from major retailers — on par with similar offerings from Aldi and Lidl.

Store workers also told Business Insider they're awash with online orders for the $35 holiday meal basket announced last month.

"The meal deal frenzy has been nuts! I work at a neighborhood market and we are still experiencing a higher volume," a worker in Oklahoma said. Walmart neighborhood markets are smaller than super centers and more focused on groceries.

Walmart workers Business Insider spoke with also attributed some of this year's surge to a new coupon code that knocks an additional $10 off the basket price for qualifying shoppers. Several codes went viral on social media last week.

"The promo code being available online only is the one that's really pushing it to being this big thing, because actually we did the same $35 basket last year," Cheyenne, an online fulfillment worker in Ohio, told Business Insider.

Online and app customers entering a discount code at checkout can see their basket drop from $35 to $25, roughly half the total price of the deal's basket of items without active promotions and discounts.

For example, shoppers who have used pickup or delivery once or twice before can use the code Double10 to get $10 off. Shoppers who haven't used the service in the past year can enter Triple10 to get the same deal. The codes may not be used with other offers or discounts, including the Walmart employee discount.

Walmart says the $35 holiday meal combo will be offered through Christmas Eve, subject to availability of actual supplies, but a FAQ page for the promotion says the $10 coupons will stop working on November 30.

Cheyenne said she started seeing mentions of the code on TikTok on Sunday before a surge in orders came on Monday and carried through the week. She said she's been handling dozens of meal combo orders every day since and hers is not an especially high-volume location.

articles.title: The Fed isn't riding to the rescue — Wall Street still sees a December rate hike after tech's worst week since 2020: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Every correction that hit with inflation speeding up this fast became a bear market, and the Fed still wants to hike.
articles.body:
The S&P 500 just lost ground for seven straight days, its first streak that long since the pandemic crash. The Fed is still expected to raise rates in less than three weeks.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 3.7% Friday and closed in a correction — 10% or more below its record — with about $8 trillion gone since that Oct. 6 peak. The Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ) sank 5.6% and is a hair's breadth from a bear market, defined as a 20% drop.

Bettors aren't counting on relief. Polymarket gives a hike at the Fed's Dec. 9 meeting about 91% odds, down from 98% on Nov. 12, and the bond market is pricing in a 92% chance. "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," Fed governor Lisa Cook said Friday .

"Anybody who has studied history knows that half the biggest market crashes in history happen on a Monday," Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management said on Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa Live . "You have a bad week, you have a horrible Friday."

Seven of the S&P 500's 10 worst days since 1952 came on a Monday. Tuesday has none of the 20 worst.

After the nine past weeks like this one — a 5% loss capped by a 3% Friday drop — the next Monday fell seven times, typically about 3%. The rest of the week usually rose, and by Friday the S&P 500 was higher seven times. The big exception was October 1987, when the next Monday became infamously known as Black Monday .

This Monday is off to a better start. S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ) and Nasdaq 100 futures ( NQ=F ) gained each gained over 2%.

Most corrections don't last. Since 1989, 12 of 16 were erased within a year.

But consumer prices rose about 4% in the year through October, by Yahoo Finance's estimate , up from about 2.8% a year earlier. Since 1950, all eight corrections from a record that hit with inflation running a point or more faster than a year before became bear markets.

Former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang faces closed-door House interviews Dec. 1 and a Senate request to testify publicly, in what could be one of Washington's biggest business hearings in years . The SEC is reportedly examining Nvidia's accounting as well as its disclosures, and the company has delayed its full quarterly filing .

The last time stocks panicked, the Fed held off. "The Fed likely would have hiked in October without the market turmoil that preceded the meeting," Natixis' Chris Hodge said this month .

Billionaire investor Bill Ackman wants a repeat. "I think the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th," he wrote on X , calling its 2% inflation target "misguided."

articles.title: CrowdStrike is spending $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler in a huge cybersecurity deal as tech outages spread
articles.summary: A big deal in cybersecurity has hit.
articles.body:
With tech outages ripping across the world, CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) is shelling out big-time money to acquire fellow cybersecurity player and longtime partner Zscaler ( ZS ).

The two will also combine businesses led by two veteran tech founders: George Kurtz at CrowdStrike and Jay Chaudhry at Zscaler.

CrowdStrike will spend $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler, it said on Monday. The company's market cap stood at $31.7 billion at Friday's close. Chaudhry will continue to lead Zscaler while also joining the board of CrowdStrike.

Shares of CrowdStrike fell 8%, while Zscaler rose 17%.

CrowdStrike said it expects revenue synergies to build progressively over the first 30 months following an expected close in mid 2027, reaching about $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue synergies by the end of that period. It sees $500 million in cost synergies within 18-24 months of the deal closing.

"We view this as the clearest signal yet that cybersecurity is consolidating into a handful of platforms, with the AI era forcing the hand of vendors who had been content to partner," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

articles.title: Nvidia stock soars as Trump makes U-turn on Jensen Huang, cheers Huang's return as CEO
articles.summary: A not-so-subtle shift in tone in the Jensen Huang saga has sent Nvidia's stock reeling this month.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock is surging after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The move came after a not-so-subtle shift in tone in the Jensen Huang saga in D.C.

Washington has gone from wanting Huang out of Nvidia in the wake of his affairs going public to wanting him back in the corner office.

Nvidia stock soared more than 30% in premarket trading on Monday, rocketing from earlier gains as President Trump explicitly called on Nvidia's board to rehire its ousted co-founder. He argued that bringing Huang back would be the best thing for the company — and for the United States.

"I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday.

On Monday, Trump cheered the board's decision to reinstate Huang.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Just days ago, Trump was floating former Apple ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook as a possible replacement.

Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also subtly changed his tune on Huang.

After demanding that Nvidia look outside the company for its next CEO, Bessent was asked on "Face the Nation" on Sunday whether Huang could return.

"Jensen is on the outside now," Bessent said. That's a clever answer, and a notable retreat from his tougher earlier position.

articles.title: Wall Street Surges Toward M&A Record as Megadeals Defy Selloff
articles.summary: Wall Street is taking a big step toward a record year for mergers and acquisitions as some of the world's largest companies defy a tech-induced selloff in gl...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street is taking a big step toward a record year for mergers and acquisitions as some of the world's largest companies defy a tech-induced selloff in global stocks to pursue major takeovers.

CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. ( CRWD ) on Monday confirmed Bloomberg News reporting that it will acquire cybersecurity provider Zscaler Inc. ( ZS ) The near $44 billion transaction highlights the shift toward a smaller number of companies protecting more of the world's computers and networks.

It's the second megadeal announced in the global technology industry this month, following Marvell Technology Inc.'s planned purchase of Lumentum Holdings Inc. for around $115 billion including debt, and comes as dealmakers work to recover from a recent slump in activity brought on in part by concerns about a new rate-hiking cycle.

Elsewhere on Monday, Texas Pacific Land Corp. struck a roughly $3 billion purchase of EagleRock Land; Var Energi ASA agreed to acquire ConocoPhillips assets in Norway and the UK for about $2.5 billion including debt; and ABB Ltd. said it will buy privately held German cooling systems company Ziehl-Abegg SE for an equity value of $2.2 billion.

The value of deals announced globally this year now sits at around $4.6 trillion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That's about $700 billion shy of a new annual record. Dealmakers' chances of passing that milestone could hinge on a clutch of multibillion-dollar transactions already being discussed across of a range of major industries.

In financial services, private equity firm GTCR is pursuing a takeover of Global Payments Inc. in what, at around $50 billion, would be one of the biggest-ever leveraged buyouts. And in healthcare, Sanofi SA is weighing an acquisition of US drugmaker Insmed Inc. in what could end up being the largest tie-up in the global biopharma sector for three years. And Clariant AG and CD&R are in talks to acquire chemicals maker Ashland Inc.

Wall Street advisers say that, following the midterm elections in the US, companies are operating under a renewed sense of urgency to chase transformative takeovers while M&A-friendly regulators remain in place under President Donald Trump.

articles.title: Arm CEO Extends Contract Through 2033 After Nvidia Approach
articles.summary: Arm Holdings Plc Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas, approached as a potential successor to Nvidia Corp.'s Jensen Huang, has extended his contract to stay in...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Arm Holdings Plc ( ARM ) Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas, approached as a potential successor to Nvidia Corp.'s ( NVDA ) Jensen Huang, has extended his contract to stay in his current role leading the chip designer through 2033.

Haas, 64, will also take on a role as vice chairman of SoftBank Group Corp., Arm's largest shareholder, starting on Dec. 1, the company said in a statement on Monday.

"I've never been more confident about Arm's future," Haas said in the statement. "I'm incredibly proud of what we're building and wholly committed to realizing Arm's full potential for many years to come."

Executive recruiting firm Heidrick & Struggles, appointed by Nvidia's board to find a successor to Huang after the chipmakers longtime CEO and co-founder was ousted, had approached Haas, who was seen as a leading contender for the job. Haas had previously served for seven years at Nvidia as general manager of computing products. Nvidia also attempted to acquire Arm in 2020, though the merger eventually broke down in the face of regulatory opposition.

articles.title: Homebuyer secured Rs 1.36 crore refund with 10.20% interest after RERA ruled in his favour, but builder challenged the order nearly 5 years later citing a Supreme Court ruling; why Bombay High Court dismissed the plea
articles.summary: You buy a flat and due to some dispute with the real estate developer, you seek a refund and the Real Estate Regulation Authority (RERA)’s adjudicating
articles.body: You buy a flat and due to some dispute with the real estate developer, you seek a refund and the Real Estate Regulation Authority (RERA)’s adjudicating officer passes an order in your favour. Years later, the developer challenges the order on the basis of a fresh Supreme Court ruling. What happens then?The Bombay High Court has dismissed a petition filed by a real estate developer which sought to set aside an order directing it to refund Rs 1.36 crore, along with interest at 10.20% per annum, to a flat purchaser.The developer argued that a subsequent Supreme Court ruling had rendered the original refund order legally invalid.The Bombay High Court rejected the developer’s plea and declined to reopen an order that had attained finality after the developer failed to challenge it within the prescribed statutory period. Read on to know what happened.What the case is aboutThe dispute arose from an order in 2019, passed by an adjudicating officer of the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority. The officer had directed the real estate developer to refund Rs 1,35,99,246 paid by a flat buyer, along with interest at 10.20% per annum until realisation.The real estate developer did not challenge the order within the prescribed statutory period for filing an appeal. Following non-compliance, a recovery order was issued in October 2021. Under the applicable mechanism, recovery of amounts ordered to be refunded under RERA could be pursued as arrears of land revenue under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966.Meanwhile in November 2021, the Supreme Court delivered its judgment in Newtech Promoters and Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh, which interpreted provisions of RERA concerning the powers of the regulatory authority and its adjudicating officers.The real estate developer subsequently argued that the ruling undermined the legal basis of the 2019 refund order. Its contention was that an adjudicating officer appointed under Section 71 of RERA could adjudicate compensation claims but could not direct a refund. On that basis, the developer sought to have both the original order and the subsequent recovery order set aside.The developer also relied on a Bombay High Court Division Bench judgment in Marveledge Realtors Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra, delivered on September 13, 2024, as well as other judicial decisions.The homebuyer opposed the petition. His counsel argued that the original order had attained finality because the developer had not filed a statutory appeal. He also pointed to the delay in approaching the High Court: although the Supreme Court had delivered its judgment in November 2021, the developer filed the present writ petition only in August, 2024.Why Bombay High Court ruled in favour of homebuyerThe Bombay High Court first examined whether the Supreme Court’s judgment in Newtech established that an adjudicating officer could never be entrusted with the power to direct a refund.The court distinguished the issue decided by the Supreme Court from the question before it.The court noted that Newtech dealt with whether a whole-time member of the regulatory authority could order a refund, rather than whether the authority could delegate that function to an adjudicating officer under Section 81 of RERA.“The Supreme Court was not dealing with a contention that the Adjudicating Officer could be delegated the power to direct a refund,” the judgment said.The court further explained that the Supreme Court’s observations had to be read in the context of the issue it had actually decided.The judgement said: “Seen in that light, in Newtech, the Supreme Court essentially held that the WTM can indeed exercise the power to direct a refund. The Supreme Court did not at all venture into what the Adjudicating Officer cannot do.”The High Court concluded that delegating the exercise of refund powers to an adjudicating officer was not contrary to RERA’s statutory scheme. It distinguished refund claims, which can involve a summary assessment based on documentary evidence, from compensation proceedings under Section 71, which require a more elaborate adjudicatory process.Delay and finality were central to the outcome.The judgement observed: “Even if one can raise the facet of jurisdiction at any stage it is well settled that closed and concluded matters cannot be reopened on the premise that a subsequent judgement of a superior court has declared the law differently.”The chronology was also significant. The High Court noted that the developer waited nearly three years after that judgment before filing the present writ petition.The court also noted that another bench was already dealing with a petition filed by the homebuyer concerning the enforcement proceedings. In the circumstances, it was unwilling to exercise the High Court’s discretionary writ jurisdiction to reopen the dispute.According to Shruti Maniar, Partner, Solomon & Co, the Bombay High Court analysed the effect of the Supreme Court judgment of Newtech for this ruling.“Although, under RERA, the power to order a refund vests in the Authority, the Authority may delegate any of its powers to its officers under Section 81. An Adjudicating Officer, being an officer of RERA, is a judicial officer to adjudicate compensation, which is a judicial function, such an officer may also perform summary functions such as directing a refund, as was done in the present case,” Maniar tells TOI.“A Writ Jurisdiction being discretionary in nature should be applied sparingly. Since the developer did not challenge the original order within the prescribed limitation period, allowing it to attain finality and the Writ Petition being filed nearly three years after Newtech, without sufficient explanation for the delay, the Writ Court rightly refused to exercise its discretionary powers,” she explains.Key takeaways from the judgementAccording to Shruti Maniar, the three lessons from the judgement are:For developers, the message is one of procedural discipline. Jurisdictional objections and challenges to adverse RERA orders must be raised without any delay or laches. A subsequent change or clarification in the legal position cannot be a fresh cause to challenge orders that have attained finality. The ruling also offers reassurance to homebuyers that any person does not suffer on account of procedural irregularity as prescribed under Section 30(b) of the RERA Act and ensures that refund orders will not necessarily become unenforceable merely because of change in law on account of later judgment passed by a superior court.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, stock rockets
articles.summary: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.body:
Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board on Monday announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant.

Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also climbed more than 30%.

In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company.

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said.

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO."

Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board.

Just last week, Jones told investors during the company's Q3 earnings call that Nvidia had no plans to bring back Huang.

"I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement.

"I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry, and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work," he added.

Huang previously resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 after an alleged affair with a woman, Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang admitted to having an affair at the time, but didn't name the woman.

He also allegedly had affairs with two Nvidia employees including executive Kimberly Powell.

Alice Huang was the executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling high-powered Nvidia chips to China.

Jensen Huang's allies, including President Trump, reportedly lobbied for his return as CEO.

In a Truth Social post, Trump lauded Huang's reinstatement.

"The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," he said.

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," Trump continued, adding he considers Huang a "Great Patriot and National Treasure."

articles.title: India weighs 20% export duty on select rice varieties to boost domestic supply: Report
articles.summary: India is considering imposing export duties of around 20 per cent on certain rice varieties to improve domestic availability and contain price increases
articles.body: India is considering imposing export duties of around 20 per cent on certain rice varieties to improve domestic availability and contain price increases faced by consumers and industries, Reuters reported, citing two government and two industry sources.The proposed measures could apply particularly to 100 per cent broken rice and some premium non-Basmati varieties that have become scarce in southern states.The government is discussing the restrictions with relevant ministries, with a final decision expected after consultations, one government source told Reuters.A government official said the Centre was considering steps to limit shipments and support domestic industries affected by rising prices."We are considering measures to limit exports and support the domestic industry," the official said.The poultry and cattle feed industries have been among the worst affected by the sharp increase in broken rice prices and have urged the government to restrict exports, another government official told Reuters.Export curbs could benefit rival suppliersIndia is the world's largest rice exporter, and any restrictions on its shipments could create opportunities for competing suppliers such as Thailand, Vietnam and Myanmar. These countries have struggled to compete with India's lower-priced supplies.A New Delhi-based dealer with a global trading house said an export duty could slow Indian shipments but was unlikely to stop them altogether, given the country's price advantage over rival exporters.The proposed restrictions are being considered against a backdrop of rising prices for some premium non-Basmati varieties, although prices of other grades have remained largely stable.Mukesh Jain, a rice exporter based in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, said domestic supplies remained comfortably above demand despite the increase in prices of certain varieties.Rice reserves at record high levelsIndia's state reserves of rice, including unmilled paddy, stood at a record 55.3 million metric tonnes as of November 1, nearly four times the government's target.Jain said there was no need to restrict exports, arguing that overseas shipments would help create storage space for the incoming crop."There is no need to restrict rice exports. Exports should continue uninterrupted to help create storage space for the new crop," he said.The government's proposed move would therefore seek to address shortages and price pressures in specific rice categories, particularly those used by the poultry and cattle feed industries, while weighing the implications for India's export trade.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week
articles.summary: Bettors gave Jensen Huang about a 3% shot at a return minutes before Nvidia's board brought him back.
articles.body:
Nvidia's board needed 12 days to hit "undo" on Jensen Huang. Three years ago this week, OpenAI needed less than five to do the same with Sam Altman.

Almost nobody saw the Huang news coming. Minutes before Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced his return Monday morning, bettors on Polymarket gave him about a 3% chance of getting his job back this month. Five minutes later, the odds were 99%.

The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO, and director, effective immediately, and to return Colette Kress to CFO. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia," Chair Harvey Jones said. Nvidia stock jumped more than 30% in premarket trading.

Nvidia lost about $1.2 trillion in market value from the Nov. 11 close, when the board accepted Huang's resignation, through Friday, a stretch that included the stock's worst week ever .

Silicon Valley has seen this movie before. OpenAI fired Altman on a Friday afternoon in November 2023. Microsoft ( MSFT ) hired him that Sunday, and more than 700 of OpenAI's roughly 770 employees threatened to follow him. By Tuesday night, he was back.

"I love OpenAI, and everything I've done over the past few days has been in service of keeping this team and its mission together," Altman wrote on X.

Huang had his own campaign, though not one he ran. A "Stand With Jensen" petition drew more than 100,000 signatures, Elon Musk's among them, including more than 5,000 from people who say they work at Nvidia. It called for "due process, not mob justice."

OpenAI's kingmaker was Microsoft. Nvidia's was the White House.

The board said input from senior levels of the US government led it to conclude that Huang poses no national security risk. President Donald Trump had pushed for Huang to get a second chance.

Huang's undoing is different from Altman's in one way. Altman came back to a new board. Huang comes back to the same chair, plus a new national security and export control committee, a search for a chief compliance officer, and an independent investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Steve Jobs resigned from Apple ( AAPL ) in September 1985 and was named interim CEO in September 1997. Apple stock rose 2% on his first day back and beat the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) by 65 percentage points over the next year.

Most famous comebacks start with a cheer from the Wall Street bleachers, but the year after has been a coin flip. Nvidia's premarket jump of 30% was more than triple the biggest first-day pop in the chart below.

articles.summary: Shares of Nvidia surged on Monday morning after the company’s board of directors reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. articles.body:
Shares of Nvidia surged on Monday morning after the company’s board of directors reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

The company’s stock opened at $167.04 per share, roughly $35.50 above where it closed on Friday, marking a 27 percent bump. As of 15 minutes after the opening bell, Nvidia’s stock was trading at $160.38.

The board reinstated Huang on Monday, less than two weeks after he resigned amid an affair scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s board chair, said in a statement .

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company,” Jones added.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, said he was “honored to return” to Nvidia and “lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.”

Huang added, “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”

President Trump praised Nvidia’s board of directors on Monday, saying it “ made the correct and proper decision” to bring Huang back.

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the president wrote on Truth Social.

Huang stepped down on Nov. 12, after The New York Times reported on his extramarital affairs — including one with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect is a Chinese spy.

But in announcing Jensen Huang’s return, Nvidia’s board of directors said it “received input from senior levels” of the federal government and is “confident” that reinstating the tech mogul “poses no national security risk.”

Trump also said Monday his administration has “no reason to believe” that Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia “poses any risk” to national security.

The president added Attorney General Todd Blanche “confirmed” the administration does not have evidence of Huang engaging in “any unlawful conduct.”

The stock market, which took heavy losses last week, also surged after Nvidia brought Jensen Huang back. As of 25 minutes after the opening bell, the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 were respectively up by roughly 1,300.70 and 291.70 points.

articles.title: Pixxel, IIT-K join hands to advance R&D in hyperspectral imaging, AI, geospatial applications

articles.body: New Delhi: Indian space startup Pixxel on Monday announced a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Indian Institute of Technology-Kanpur (IIT Kanpur) to advance research and development in hyperspectral imaging, artificial intelligence, and geospatial applications.The collaboration was formally announced at the India International Space Conference (IISC) 2026 in New Delhi, with Prof Sambit Behera, representing IIT Kanpur, and Group Captain Debashish Sengupta (Retd), director of govt sales, representing Pixxel, signing the MoU.The partnership brings together Pixxel's commercial satellite imaging capabilities and IIT Kanpur's scientific expertise to develop and validate advanced remote sensing models, improve the interpretation of Earth observation data, and translate academic research into practical geospatial solutions.Awais Ahmed, founder and CEO of Pixxel, said, “India has an incredible depth of scientific and engineering talent, and there's a real opportunity to bring more of that expertise into the country's growing commercial space ecosystem. As we build increasingly sophisticated capabilities in space, we also need to invest in the knowledge, talent, and partnerships that will help us make the most of them. Working with institutions like IIT Kanpur is an important part of that journey, and we're excited about what we can build together.”Under the MoU, the two organisations will focus their joint research and development efforts on three key areas: Hyperspectral algorithms & AI model development, earth surface dynamics and water resources and multi-sensor integration & data fusion.The collaboration will also strengthen research and knowledge exchange between the two organisations. Pixxel will provide access to selected hyperspectral datasets and software tools, while IIT Kanpur will contribute its expertise in algorithm development and scientific validation. Both organisations intend to pursue opportunities for joint research, funding, and scientific publications, as well as technical workshops, student internships, and jointly supervised academic projects. These efforts aim to bridge academic research and industry applications while developing the next generation of talent in Earth observation and geospatial technologies.Prof. Rajiv Sinha at IIT Kanpur said, “We look forward to developing an active collaboration with Pixxel across multiple areas of natural resource management. IIT Kanpur has an active research group on high-resolution hyperspectral remote sensing, and we have undertaken several projects in this area over the last few years. This MoU brings us one step closer to translating our ideas into action and exploring the new geospatial dataset for the benefit of the nation and society.”Earlier this year, Pixxel raised $100 million in Series C Funding, bringing its total capital raised to $195 million and making it the country’s highest-funded space tech startup. The funding will accelerate Pixxel's plans to scale its planetary infrastructure, spanning advanced satellite constellations, Earth intelligence software, and satellite manufacturing capabilities.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic stock falls as Monday's tech rally takes off
articles.summary: Just two days after its public debut, the stock market's newest AI giant, Anthropic, is missing out on Monday's major tech rally.
articles.body:
Just two days after its public debut, the stock market's newest AI giant, Anthropic ( ANT ), looks to be missing out on Monday's major tech rally.

The stock of the Claude model maker fell 1.4% on Monday, trading below $88 as of 3:00 p.m. ET after whipsawing earlier in the day. Meanwhile, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other AI-linked stocks, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ), soared amid the broader tech rebound that followed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.

The move comes after Anthropic's stock sank 9% on Friday following a 17% gain on its IPO day last Thursday. At Monday's current price, the stock is up about 5% from its $83 IPO price.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

The choppy performance might reflect ordinary post IPO profit-taking and broader skepticism about Anthropic's valuation. Needham analysts said in a Sunday note that the most common concern they hear from investors is whether the company can sustain its enormous revenue growth next year. The company's fully diluted IPO valuation of about $1.5 trillion is roughly 40 times trailing sales.

The stock also has a potential supply overhang. As much as 315 million shares held by insiders, roughly one-third of the stock the company issued in its IPO, became eligible for sale almost immediately, according to Anthropic's IPO paperwork.

Needham added that given Anthropic's staggered schedule for permitting insider share sales could bring more shares to market in the first six months.

Another key question hanging over the company is how credit markets will absorb the AI firm's massive spending needs. Anthropic has committed to spending about $900 billion on its computing and infrastructure needs for the next two decades , including $70 billion due over the next 12 months.

The AI boom's ravenous capital needs have flooded the bond market this year, becoming a looming concern for investors.

Investors expect the major rating agencies to assign a high-yield, or junk, rating to the company's debt, according to a Wall Street Journal report . No rating has yet been announced.

Anthropic's credit rating is key for the wider AI ecosystem. Getting the higher investment-grade rating would help offer some relief to chip makers, including Nvidia and Broadcom ( AVGO ), that have guaranteed billions of dollars worth of microchips to customers that lease compute power to major model makers like Anthropic and rival OpenAI. ( OPAI.PVT )

The high-yield bond market also comes with constraints, including smaller capacity and higher borrowing rates, for the newly public giant.

articles.title: Nvidia’s $1.5 trillion boardroom blunder helped bring Jensen Huang back
articles.summary: Nvidia’s intense boardroom drama, in which Jensen Huang was ousted and brought back in the span of less than two weeks, would not have been possible without questionable decisions by Nvidia’s directors.
articles.body: Nvidia’s intense boardroom drama, in which Jensen Huang was ousted and brought back in the span of less than two weeks, would not have been possible without questionable decisions by Nvidia’s directors. Now, the board faces intense scrutiny over its role in a corporate soap opera with enormous consequences. While Wall Street loves the shocking return of Huang at the helm of Nvidia, corporate governance experts are horrified by what they view as malpractice by the company’s board: With no chair prior to Huang’s ouster, no succession plan and the loosest of leashes on its CEO, the board had set itself up to fail. Huang said he built the company so that he alone could run it – and the stock acted that way, losing $1.5 trillion in market value since the scandal erupted on Nov. 8. An outpouring of support for Huang from investors and partners followed, and a shareholder revolt seemed imminent. The board, consisting of many long-tenured Huang supporters, announced its decision to reinstate Huang on Monday, after the same board unanimously accepted his resignation. And directors are bringing Huang back before the completion of a board-ordered investigation that was supposed to get to the bottom of allegations over whether Huang has been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” President Donald Trump on Monday told CNBC he called the board and helped orchestrate Huang’s return. That put the board in a no-win scenario: Stand pat and risk getting ousted. Give in and appear weak and ineffective. (Nvidia declined to comment.) Of course, it didn’t have to be this way. A strong board – one that provides vigorous oversight of the CEO and requires successors to be groomed – could have avoided this mess turning into a debacle. “The board should resign. Every one of them,” said Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management. “This is a complete failure of corporate governance.” Backed into a corner Huang stands accused of some serious violations of corporate policy. He acknowledged an affair after reports of a relationship with a major customer, and he was reportedly in a relationship with an employee. Although the board on Monday said US government officials assured them rehiring Huang posed no national security risk, the investigation continues. The seriousness of the allegations make Huang’s return all the more shocking from a corporate governance standpoint. “The standard to apply is: Would we fire a middle manager for this behavior?” said Nell Minow, chair of corporate governance advisory firm ValueEdge Advisors. Potential espionage aside, Huang’s affairs would be grounds for dismissal, Minow argued. Minow said she would favor the board resigning except that she fears Huang would just bring in people who are “even more compliant.” But the board appears to have been backed into a corner. The Nvidia scandal contributed to a market meltdown so severe that some suggested the AI bubble was popping before our eyes. Huang was the He-Man CEO of AI, the industry’s de facto central banker and widely viewed as a visionary pioneer who transformed graphics processors into the lifeblood of AI computing. And he is buddies with the president of the United States. Trump on Monday was effusive with praise for Huang, telling CNBC he personally called Huang and the board to help arrange his comeback. “With pressure from the president and his administration, the board may have felt it had no choice, but this is not a board that has ever shown that it understands its obligations to shareholders or to the law,” Minow said. The board failed by placing Huang above corporate governance, said Bill George, former CEO of Medtronic. “The board does not appear to be in control,” said George, now an executive fellow at Harvard Business School. The invincible CEO The board didn’t have to let it get to this point. For example, it could have opted to put Huang on leave pending the results of the investigation, which could have insulated it from outside pressure – even from the commander in chief. But the problems started earlier. Without a succession plan, Huang effectively held the board hostage, said Sonnenfeld, the Yale professor. Most well-run companies with functional boards have an emergency plan in place, in case the CEO is hit by a bus, suddenly resigns or needs to be disciplined. They also typically review potential replacement CEO candidates as part of their due diligence. There’s no evidence Nvidia had done any of that. That, in part, gave Huang an aura of invincibility. “Our company was built so that I know how to run it,” Huang told Bloomberg in 2023. “So, for as long as I’m running it, that’s all that matters.” Nvidia has a deeply talented bench. So allowing a company to rely on a singular figure – who alone could account for trillions of dollars of company value – represents a complete failure of the board, Sonnenfeld argued. Still, the board’s flip-flop may not be nefarious. Ultimately, the board is tasked with deciding whether it can trust Huang and whether his ongoing presence at Nvidia is in the best interest of the company and its stockholders, noted Brittany Rogers, partner in the corporate governance practice at O’Melveny & Myers. “There is no single ‘right’ answer here,” she said, calling the decision complex and difficult. Although it may be easy to assign bad motives to the decision to rehire Huang, the board may also have been presented with new facts that changed its mind – even from a week earlier. “I would apply the presumptions of the business judgment rule and assume that the directors acted on an informed basis, in good faith, and in the honest belief that each decision served Nvidia’s best interests,” said Lawrence Cunningham, director of the University of Delaware’s Weinberg Center for Corporate Governance.

articles.title: Democrats, angered by Huang’s return to Nvidia, vow investigations, legislation
articles.summary: Lawmakers in both parties are clamoring for answers after Nvidia’s stunning move to reinstate Jensen Huang at the top of the company, voicing concerns that he poses a national security risk in America’s race with China for global AI dominance. “Though the NVIDIA Board of Directors may be convinced that reinstating Mr. Huang ‘poses no…
articles.body:
Lawmakers in both parties are clamoring for answers after Nvidia’s stunning move to reinstate Jensen Huang at the top of the company, voicing concerns that he poses a national security risk in America’s race with China for global AI dominance.

“Though the NVIDIA Board of Directors may be convinced that reinstating Mr. Huang ‘poses no national security risk,’ the Congress still has questions that require answers,” said Rep. Jim Himes (Conn.), the senior Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, Monday in a statement.

“His reinstatement does not change the fact that we expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week.”

Huang is scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Intelligence Committee and the House Select Committee on China on Dec. 1. The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang’s testimony for Dec. 3.

Other top Democrats said Huang’s return to Nvidia creates new urgency for Congress to act, not only to investigate Huang’s ties to China, but also to move legislation to tighten U.S. export controls designed to prevent Beijing from accessing America’s most state-of-the-art computer chips.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) argued that the Trump administration’s “push” to reinstate Huang “underscores the need for Congress to act.”

“Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he’s learned nothing from his resounding election defeat. Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” Schumer said. “We’ll also work on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.”

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) said in a statement that Congress “will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.”

Lawmakers across the aisle have introduced legislation to tighten restrictions on chip exports, but it remains unclear whether there is appetite to take up the proposals in the lame-duck session. A bipartisan group of lawmakers is hoping to include chip export controls in the National Defense Authorization Act.

“We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump Administration for personal financial gain. The National Defense Authorization Act must include ironclad export control legislation to prevent powerful AI technology from being exploited by the Chinese Communist Party and other adversaries. It’s time for traditional Republicans in Congress to join us in reining in this corruption,” Jeffries said in a statement.

Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia, the chip-making behemoth, resigned as CEO on Nov. 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs with a company executive and a Chinese tech executive suspected of spying for Beijing.

The decision by Nvidia’s board to return Huang to power came amid heavy pressure from President Trump to do just that. Afterward, Trump wasted no time taking credit.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them,” Trump told CNBC . “I made the deal.”

Trump also said he gave Nvidia’s board “assurances” that Huang poses no national security threat, and warned that not returning Huang as CEO might push him to work for China directly.

“People say, is it a threat to have him?” Trump told CNBC. “No, it’s a threat to lose him.”

The China hawks on Capitol Hill have decidedly different views. They’re worried that Huang, who has long pushed to sell Nvidia chips to China, is undermining America’s advantage in the AI race.

“Jensen Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China,” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) said. “We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible.”

“Ummm… she was, and is, a spy,” Rep. Bill Huizenga (R-Mich.) wrote on the social platform X. “How about we get serious about making sure China doesn’t steal US company technology? Or get serious about not selling it directly and indirectly?”

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) wrote on X that, “The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high and probably for some f‑‑‑ing donation to his ballroom.”

Himes suggested Monday that his previously scheduled meetings with congressional panels are still on.

And other top Democrats said they want to expand the investigation to include Trump officials, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who reportedly took a softer tone on Nvidia over the company’s AI chip sales to China and failed to put the Singaporean firm Megaspeed on the trade entity blacklist. They’re vowing to do just that when they take control of the gavels in the next Congress.

“Why are Trump and Lutnick putting China’s interests first? Is it just the tens and hundreds of millions of dollars they’re making out in the open or does Huang have even more damning information on them?” said Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), who’s in line to chair the House Judiciary Committee next year, in a statement.

Democrats are hardly alone in their misgivings about Huang and his return to the top of Nvidia. Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.), who sits on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told The Hill he wants more answers around Huang’s alleged relationship with the Chinese spy.

“Did he know she was a spy?” Fine said. “I assume the answer to that’s going to be no. What did he tell her? You know, he may say, ‘Well, I didn’t tell her anything.’ You know … I’ll ask that, and that’s the first set of information I want to know.”

“And then the second set is about the risk with China. We are in an AI arms race with China, and China is winning some parts of it, and we’re winning some parts of it. And China is at war with us right now over it … we don’t want to sell China the chips because it’s a four-tiered war. It’s software that we’re winning, chips that we’re winning, energy infrastructure that we’re losing, and data centers, which right now is unclear,” Fine added, noting that whoever wins this “war” will determine who wins the 21st century.

Julia Shapero and Miranda Nazzaro contributed.

articles.title: What happens when your bank goes offline? How to protect your money
articles.summary: Banking outages can disrupt payments, transfers and access to accounts.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — As Americans increasingly rely on digital banking, technology outages can leave customers unable to access their accounts, transfer money or make payments.

Technical problems can affect banking websites, mobile apps, ATMs and payment services, creating problems for customers trying to pay bills and access their money.

While disruptions are often temporary, financial experts recommend having backup payment options and taking precautions to avoid fees, fraud and missed payments.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

What should you do if your bank goes offline?

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) recommends contacting your bank or credit union to determine which services are affected and when they are expected to be restored.

If mobile or online banking is unavailable, customers may still be able to access their accounts through ATMs, telephone banking or in-person branches, depending on the outage.

The CFPB also recommends checking whether automatic payments and withdrawals are still being processed.

Customers should avoid repeatedly submitting transactions when their status is unclear because doing so could result in duplicate payments once services are restored.

Consumers should also keep records of unsuccessful transactions, including receipts, payment attempts and any fees incurred during an outage, according to MadameNoire .

Having documentation can make it easier to dispute charges or request refunds once banking services are restored.

Is your money safe during a bank outage?

A temporary banking outage does not necessarily mean customers’ deposits are missing or that their accounts have been compromised.

Money deposited at an FDIC-insured bank remains eligible for federal deposit insurance even when online services are unavailable.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. generally protects eligible deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership if a bank fails.

However, deposit insurance does not guarantee uninterrupted access to banking services during a technical outage.

How can you prepare for the next bank outage?

Financial experts recommend having more than one way to access money in case a bank or payment service becomes unavailable.

Keeping a backup credit or debit card from another financial institution can provide another payment option if a primary bank experiences technical difficulties.

Consumers may also consider keeping a small amount of emergency cash in a secure location for purchases when electronic payments are unavailable.

Maintaining an emergency savings account at a separate bank can provide another source of funds, although transfers between financial institutions may not be immediate.

Experts also recommend keeping records of recurring bills, payment due dates and customer service contact information.

What if a bank outage causes missed payments or fees?

Customers who are charged late fees, overdraft fees or insufficient funds fees because of a banking disruption can ask their financial institutions to reverse the charges.

According to the CFPB , consumers should contact the company responsible for the fee and explain how the outage prevented them from making a payment.

Fee reversals are not guaranteed, but customers can explain how the disruption affected their transactions and provide documentation.

If a payment deadline is approaching, customers should contact the company they owe to discuss alternative payment arrangements.

Can banking outages increase the risk of scams?

Banking disruptions can create opportunities for scammers to impersonate financial institutions and send fraudulent messages about account access.

The Gate City Bank recommends using strong, unique passwords, enabling multifactor authentication and setting up transaction alerts to help protect accounts.

The bank also advises customers to verify suspicious messages through trusted contact information rather than clicking unfamiliar links.

The CFPB recommends contacting banks through verified customer service numbers rather than responding to unexpected texts, emails or phone calls requesting account information.

Customers should also monitor their accounts once services are restored and report any unfamiliar transactions.

A system outage does not necessarily mean a bank has experienced a cyberattack or that customer data has been compromised.

Michael McCaul (R-Texas), a former chair of the House Homeland Security Committee, pressed for a briefing from the Trump administration on Jensen Huang’s return to his role as Nvidia CEO. “If administration officials now believe that Mr. Huang’s extramarital relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset — along with Nvidia’s deeply concerning sales of…
articles.body:
Rep. Michael McCaul (R-Texas), a former chair of the House Homeland Security Committee, pressed for a briefing from the Trump administration on Jensen Huang’s return to his role as Nvidia CEO.

“If administration officials now believe that Mr. Huang’s extramarital relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset — along with Nvidia’s deeply concerning sales of advanced chips to Megaspeed — no longer poses a national security threat, then they need to brief Congress immediately and release as much information as possible to the public,” McCaul wrote on social media Monday afternoon.

“The American people deserve full transparency when it comes to safeguarding U.S. national security,” McCaul added.

Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO a little more than a week after he stepped down amid an affair scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s board chair, said in a statement Monday.

Earlier this month, Huang resigned after admitting to an extramarital affair. According to reports, Huang had an affair with a woman who American officials believed was handing over information to China.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement.

The board of directors at Nvidia unanimously voted to have Huang return in the wake of a series of meetings with the tech mogul. Following those meetings, the board said they were satisfied with Huang’s “candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” per a press release.

“Senior levels” of the U.S. government also offered input to the board, with the board saying it was confident Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.

President Trump, an ally of Huang’s, lauded the board for Huang’s reinstatement, saying it “made the correct and proper decision.”

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump said on Truth Social.

“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” Trump continued

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

The company’s stock closed at $165.05 per share, marking an increase of nearly 31.5 percent from Friday’s closing bell. Nvidia closed at $125.53 per share on Friday, the stock’s lowest point since…
articles.body:
Nvidia’s stock surged on Monday after Jensen Huang returned to the company , with the tech CEO set to benefit financially from the boost.

The company’s stock closed at $165.05 per share, marking an increase of nearly 31.5 percent from Friday’s closing bell. Nvidia closed at $125.53 per share on Friday, the stock’s lowest point since May 2025.

Huang owned more than 811.5 million shares of the company’s stock as of mid-September, according to a report he filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

When Nvidia’s stock hit an all-time high of $243.37 per share on Oct. 6, Huang’s shares were worth nearly $197.5 billion.

But his shares lost nearly $100 billion in value amid the stock’s slide, which centered on reports of his extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy — and his resignation as CEO on Nov. 12.

With Huang’s return on Monday, his shares did not return to their Oct. 6 high. But they regained a portion of their value, rising to a total worth of about $133.9 billion at the closing bell.

Huang said Monday in a statement he was “honored” to return to Nvidia, which he co-founded in 1993 and oversaw en route to becoming one of the top faces of the artificial intelligence industry.

The Nvidia CEO called the company, whose chips power AI, one of the “most consequential technology companies” in the world.

“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang added. “Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

articles.title: Best Buy Q3 earnings preview: What Wall Street expects from new CEO Jason Bonfig amid crucial holiday season
articles.summary: Best Buy's new CEO stepped into the role in late October. He faces his first earnings test on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Best Buy is set to report its third quarter earnings results in the midst of the most critical shopping season for retailers. This also marks Jason Bonfig's first quarterly results as chief executive.

In the third quarter, Wall Street expects the company to post same-store sales growth of 2.3%, down slightly from the 2.7% growth reported this time last year.

Revenue is forecast to come in at $9.9 billion, up 2% from the $9.7 billion posted in Q3 last year, and adjusted earnings are expected to come in at $1.49 per share, ahead of the $1.40 reported a year ago.

The electronics retailer could see a sales boost as consumers replace their devices and seek the latest innovations. However, it is also up against a tougher macroeconomic backdrop, where factors like the war in Iran and the AI boom, which is driving memory prices higher, are increasing costs and pressuring consumers.

"Best Buy continues to execute well and maintain/gain market share in consumer electronics, driven by its ability to introduce newness, leverage scale and vendor relationships, manage costs, and operate efficiently," Telsey Advisory Group analyst Joe Feldman wrote in a note to clients.

Bonfig became Best Buy's CEO on Oct. 31, replacing Corie Barry, who held the role for more than seven years. The electronics retailer has been hitting a stride so far this year, with the stock up by around 45%.

Feldman expects broad sales momentum in mobile phones, major appliances, and emerging categories such as AI glasses, Pokémon collectible trading cards, and wearable rings.

All segments are expected to post gains, led by the services business. Wall Street expects services sales to grow 4.7%, followed by entertainment at 3.5%. Computing and mobile phone sales — which include those for the new Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone Duo — are expected to increase by 3.3%.

Last quarter, Best Buy said computing was the largest contributor to comparable sales growth, with sales jumping 6.8%. Due to higher memory costs, the company raised computing prices by a mid-teens percentage, and unit sales declined by a high-single-digit percentage.

On Sept. 16, Pokémon launched its 30th anniversary Pokémon Trading Card Game set, and Placer.ai found that visits that day were 19.9% higher than the average Wednesday.

Best Buy said in the second quarter that it expects full-year revenue to be between $42.3 billion and $42.8 billion. The company also expects sales to rise in the range of 1.9% to 3.0%, assuming a similar level of tariff refunds in the third quarter as in the second quarter.

articles.body:
Huang’s return powers stock market rally

The stock market roared back to life on Monday, buoyed by Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up by roughly 3 percent from the end of trading on Friday, a week defined by heavy losses on Wall Street.

The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 were also on the upswing, respectively rising by about 4.7 percent and 6.5 percent from the end of last week. Both indices posted their best single day since April 2025 , CNBC reported.

Huang’s return on Monday, less than two weeks after he resigned as CEO of the chipmaking giant he co-founded, marked an about-face for Nvidia’s board of directors .

As recently as last Tuesday, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said the company did “not intend to reinstate” Huang as CEO.

But President Trump and Vice President Vance personally advocated for the board to bring Huang back , with the latter leveraging his Silicon Valley ties to do so.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump said Monday on CNBC, referring to Nvidia’s board. “And I convinced them .”

Tech analyst Dan Ives wrote Monday on the social platform X the “pressure” for the board to bring Huang back “was too much” to ignore. Ives wrote last week there was “no chance” of the Nvidia co-founder returning as CEO.

Nvidia’s stock also surged on Monday, after it closed out last week at $125.53 per share — its lowest point since May 2025. Nvidia closed out Monday at $165.05 per share , an increase of nearly 31.5 percent from Friday’s closing bell.

Richard Haass , the former president of the Council on Foreign Relations, argued Monday the “political intervention” and “awful board governance” that defined Huang’s departure and return will lead to a “market collapse” surrounding Nvidia.

Stock prices “may be flying today,” Haass wrote on X, but “over time, Nvidia (in addition to the [national] security [cost]) is a recipe for a loss of confidence .”

articles.title: US adds Megaspeed, firm at centre of Nvidia scandal, to export control list
articles.summary: Bureau of Security and Industry adds Singapore-based firm and six other entities to export control list.
articles.body:
The United States has added the Singapore-based company at the centre of the alleged spying scandal involving Nvidia to its trade blacklist.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Megaspeed International and six other firms based in Southeast Asia on its Entity List on Monday, hours after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO in a stunning comeback that sent tech stocks soaring.

Megaspeed and the six other entities were determined to be “acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States”, BIS, which sits under the US Department of Commerce, said in a filing to the Federal Register.

The designations mean that anyone seeking to ship the firms advanced US technology, including Nvidia’s top-end graphics processing units (GPUs) used to train and run AI, must first obtain an export licence.

Megaspeed’s blacklisting comes as divisions in US President Donald Trump’s administration over China’s access to Nvidia chips have been laid bare in recent weeks amid claims Huang was romantically involved with a women accused of working with Chinese intelligence.

While US officials have been scrutinsing Megaspeed’s compliance with export controls for years, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department had declined to place the company on its trade blacklist, prompting recriminations from administration officials known to hold more hawkish views on China, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Trump on Monday played down the national security concerns around the Nvidia as he confirmed that he had personally intervened with the company’s board of director to push for Huang’s reinstatement, telling CNBC he felt “very strongly” about the issue.

US officials have accused Megaspeed International’s former top executive Alice Huang of working with China’s Ministry of State Security to target Huang in an intelligence-gathering operation.

Beijing has rejected the claims as “groundless speculation” and “an attempt to smear and malign China.”

The other six entities added to Washington’s entity list are MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International and Speedmatrix, based in Malaysia; Apex Enterprise Solutions and Swiftdata, based in Singapore; and Megaspeed, based in Thailand.

Malaysia’s Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, Singapore’s Ministry of Digital Development and Information, and Thailand’s Ministry of Industry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Megaspeed International, which is under investigation by the US Department of Justice on suspicion of diverting high-end chips to China in violation of export controls, did not respond to a request for comment.

The Singapore-based data centre company has previously insisted that it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and that media reports about its operations contained claims that were “not supported by verifiable evidence.”

Shiva Rajgopal, a professor of accounting at Columbia Business School, said it was “extraordinary” that the Trump administration had decided to blacklist Megaspeed while also pushing for Huang’s reinstatement.

“The board reinstated its CEO before the investigations into Megaspeed and his ties to it have concluded. Today’s listing shows those concerns are serious and unresolved,” Rajgopal told Al Jazeera.

“For the chip industry, the lesson is that knowing your customer is now a board-level issue,” Rajgopal said.

articles.title: Tata Steel to buy promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday said it has executed an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 15,510 crore and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday said it has executed an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 15,510 crore and plans to take over another 26% in the pipes and tubes maker through an open offer of Rs 16,756 crore, a move that will increase the Tata group firm's downstream production capabilities three times.The deal will enable Tata Steel to expand steel tubes and colour-coated products output to 7.5 million tonnes per annum, from 2.5 MTPA at present. The announcement came a day after the Tata Steel board approved the sale of its steel tubes and pipes business as well as Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes for about Rs 28,000 crore.In a press statement on Monday, Tata Steel said the agreement has been signed between Tata Steel and SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd (SG Spectra), a company associated with the promoter group of APL Apollo, to set up an exclusive contract.Subsequently, Tata Steel will also make an open offer for an additional 26% stake in APL Apollo Tubes at Rs 2,301.4 per share, taking the total consideration to Rs 16,756 crore. On the objectives and impact of the proposed deals, Tata Steel said the transactions will strengthen the company's downstream platform through the addition of value-added products.
